The pronoun in (مثله) refers to (الفلك). Either "the like" is meant to be what they afterwards manufactured of means of riding, or it is restricted to camels, because they used to call them "ships of the desert"; and there are other views, to which one is referred in the longer works. (وَإِنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (نشأ) is the protasis, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (we); (نغرقهم) is the apodosis; the fāʾ is a conjunction, though Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred it to be resumptive, which entails a break in the speech; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (صريخ) is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa; (لهم) is its khabar; the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause (ينقذون) is the khabar, (ينقذون) being an imperfect verb in the nominative by the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw the deputy agent. (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَمَتاعاً إِلى حِينٍ): (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (رحمة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), so it is a "emptied" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of reasons. It was also said to be a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); it was said to be a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; and it was said to be accusative by removal of the preposition. (متاعا) is conjoined to (رحمة), and (إلى حين) is an adjective. The meaning of this speech will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّقُوا ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَما خَلْفَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ): A resumptive speech, delivered to explain their turning away from these signs mentioned above. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition; the clause (قيل) is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (لهم) is attached to (قيل); the clause (اتقوا) is the content of the saying; (اتقوا) is an imperative verb and an agent; (ما) is a direct object; the adverbial is attached to an omitted ṣila of (ما); (أيديكم) is a muḍāf ilayhi; (وما خلفكم) is conjoined to (ما بين أيديكم); (لعلكم) is (لعل) and its noun; and the clause (ترحمون) is its khabar. The apodosis of (إذا) is omitted, indicated by what comes next, the implied form being "aʿraḍū wa-ashāḥū" (they turned away and averted themselves). (وَما تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آياتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كانُوا عَنْها مُعْرِضِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (تأتيهم) is an imperfect verb and a direct object; (من) is a redundant preposition and (آية) is genitive in form but nominative in position as agent; (من آيات ربهم) is an adjective, and the meaning of (من) is partitive; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; the clause (كانوا عنها معرضين) is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; (كان) and its noun; (عنها) is attached to (معرضين); and (معرضين) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم» up to His saying: «ومتاعا إلى حين» there is salāmat al-ikhtirāʿ (soundness of invention), which is bringing a meaning that has not been preceded in. Their rescue from drowning by a mercy from Him, Exalted is He, is in itself an enjoyment they enjoy, but it is in every case until a determined term in which they die and from which they have no escape. So if they are saved from drowning they will not be saved from what resembles or approaches it, and in death there is no difference. Abū al-Ṭayyib, as is his habit, looked up toward the heaven of this meaning and said, in a poem he composed in Egypt, in which he mentions the fever that used to visit him:
وإن أسلم فما أبقى ولكن ... سلمت من الحمام إلى الحمام
(Though I survive, I will not remain; I have only been spared from one death to another death.)
He says: if I am spared from an illness I will not remain forever, but I have been spared from death by this illness to death by another illness. This is a wonderful meaning which the poets have passed around, and another said:
إذا بلّ من داء به خال أنه ... تجاذبه الداء الذي هو قاتله
(When he recovers from an ailment he thinks that the very ailment that will kill him is pulling at him.)
Abū al-Ṭayyib hummed [around] depicting hurried enjoyment in two verses and did not rise to the verse:
تمتع من سهاد أو رقاد ... ولا تأمل كرى تحت الرجام
فإن لثالث الحالين معنى ... سوى معنى انتباهك والمنام
(Enjoy wakefulness or sleep, but do not hope for slumber beneath the stones of the grave; for the third of the two states has a meaning other than the meaning of your waking and your sleeping.)
By "the third of the two states" he meant death. He says: so long as you are alive, enjoy the two states of sleeping and wakefulness, for you will not sleep in the grave; death is other than waking and slumber, so do not think death is sleep.

* Benefits:
The words of al-Qurṭubī in the commentary on the verse:
We promised you that we would transmit to you the words of al-Qurṭubī, and in fulfilment of this promise we give them to you: "This verse is among the most difficult in this sura, because they are the ones who are carried. So it was said: the meaning is 'a sign for the people of Mecca is that We carried the descendants of past generations in the laden ship', so the two pronouns differ. Al-Mahdawī mentioned this, and al-Naḥḥās related it from ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, that he heard him say it. It was also said that both pronouns are for the people of Mecca, on the basis that what is meant by their dhurriyyāt is their children and their weak ones; the ship (al-fulk) on the first view is the ship of Nūḥ, and on the second it is a generic noun. Allah the Exalted tells, of His kindness and His favour, that He created ships in which are carried those who are too weak to walk and ride, of the children and the weak, so the two pronouns on this are in agreement. It was also said that dhurriyya means the fathers and grandfathers whom Allah the Exalted carried in the ship of Nūḥ, peace be upon him; so the fathers are dhurriyya and the sons are dhurriyya, by evidence of this verse, said Abū ʿUthmān; the fathers were called dhurriyya because the sons were begotten (dhuriʾa) from them. A fourth view is that the dhurriyya is the sperm-drops (nuṭaf), which Allah the Exalted carried in the wombs of women, likening them to the laden ship; this was said by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and mentioned by al-Māwardī." The sound and well-founded view is what we have already presented.

dervis-irab:77-83.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَصِيمٌ): an adversary, a disputant; and khuṣūma is dispute. He said in al-Qāmūs:
"khāṣamahu mukhāṣamatan wa-khuṣūmatan, then khaṣamahu yakhṣimuhu: he overcame him, and it is irregular, because for fāʿaltuhu followed by faʿaltuhu, the imperfect returns to the ḍamma unless its middle letter is a guttural, in which case it takes the fatḥa, like fākhartuhu, then fakhartuhu yafkhuruhu; as for the weak verbs like wajadtu and biʿtu, they return to the kasra, except those with a wāw, which return to the ḍamma, like rāḍaytuhu, then raḍawtuhu arḍūhu, and khāwafanī, then khiftuhu akhūfuhu; and this is not said of everything, for one does not say nāzaʿtuhu (and then naziʿtuhu), because they dispensed with it by ghalabtuhu. Ikhtaṣamū and takhāṣamū: they disputed. Al-khaṣm is the disputant, the plural khuṣūm, and it may be used for two, for the plural and for the feminine; al-khaṣīm is the disputant, the plural khuṣamāʾ and khaṣmān; and rajul khaṣim, like fariḥ: a disputer, the plural khaṣimūn. Whoever read «وهم يخصمون» meant yakhtaṣimūna, so he turned the tāʾ into ṣād, assimilated it and transferred its vowel to the khāʾ; some do not transfer it and put a kasra on the khāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; Abū ʿAmr slurs the vowel of the khāʾ; as for joining two quiescent letters, that is an error. Al-khuṣm with a ḍamma is the side, the corner and the region, and the end of the corner opposite the ʿazlāʾ (the mouth of a water-skin) at its back; the plural is akhṣām and khuṣūm; and the akhṣām of the eye are what the eyelids are joined to." We have quoted this entry at its full length for its usefulness and to show you the extent of the error that the author of al-Munjid fell into, for he confused it strangely and made al-akhṣām a plural of al-khaṣm and al-khaṣīm, and it is, as you have seen, one of the errors of this wonderful book!!
(رَمِيمٌ): decayed; and in al-Mukhtār: "ramma (with a fatḥa) yarimmu (with a kasra) when it decays, and its chapter is ḍaraba." So it is a noun, not an adjective, and therefore it is not made feminine, though it occurs as a khabar of a feminine; and it is not faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil or mafʿūl. The clarification of this statement is that faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil does not take the tāʾ in its feminine unless it remains adjectival, while what is here has been stripped of that and has come to be predominantly a noun, that is, it became, by predominance, a noun for bones that have decayed.

* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الْإِنْسانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْناهُ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ فَإِذا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ): a resumptive clause, brought to denounce their denial of the resurrection; al-Zamakhsharī excelled in establishing this meaning, as will come in the section on benefits. The hamza is for rhetorical denial and wonder; the wāw is a conjunction, which has been discussed at length; lam is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; yara is an imperfect verb jussive by lam, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the weak letter; al-insānu is the fāʿil (agent); annā and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of yara, because the seeing here is one of knowledge; anna and its noun, and the clause khalaqnāhu is its khabar (predicate); khalaqnāhu is a verb, fāʿil and direct object; min nuṭfatin is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to khalaqnāhu; the fā is a conjunction, idhā is a particle of surprise, huwa is a mubtadaʾ (subject), khaṣīmun is the khabar and mubīnun an adjective; and the clause idhā huwa khaṣīmun mubīnun is conjoined to the clause lam yara al-insānu, entering with it within the scope of denial and wonder. (وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلًا وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, ḍaraba is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; lanā are two words attached to ḍaraba, and mathalan is a direct object; nasiya is conjoined to ḍaraba and khalqahu is a direct object; the conjunction enters within the scope of wonder and denial; or the wāw is circumstantial with an implied qad, that is, "when he has forgotten his creation".
(قالَ مَنْ يُحْيِ الْعِظامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ): man is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause yuḥyī al-ʿiẓāma is its khabar; the wāw is circumstantial, hiya is a mubtadaʾ and ramīmun a khabar; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا الَّذِي أَنْشَأَها أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ): the clause yuḥyīhā is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); it is an imperfect verb with a direct object, and alladhī is the fāʿil, and the clause ansha'ahā is a ṣila (relative clause); awwala marratin is accusative as an adverbial attached to anshaʾahā; the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial, huwa is a mubtadaʾ, bi-kulli are two words attached to ʿalīmun, and ʿalīmun is the khabar of huwa. (الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ ناراً فَإِذا أَنْتُمْ مِنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ): alladhī is a badal (substitute) of the preceding alladhī, the clause jaʿala is a ṣila, and lakum is in the position of the second object; min al-shajari al-akhḍari is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of nāran; nāran is the first object of jaʿala; fa-idhā: the fā is a conjunction and idhā is a particle of surprise; antum is a mubtadaʾ, minhu are two words attached to tūqidūna, and the clause tūqidūna is the khabar of antum.
(أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ): the hamza is for rhetorical denial, and the wāw is a conjunction to an implied clause that the situation requires, that is, "Is not the One who brought them into being the first time, and is not the One who made for you fire from the green tree, and is not the One who created the heavens and the earth able...?" laysa is a defective past verb, alladhī is its noun, and the clause khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-al-arḍa is a ṣila; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and qādirin is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of laysa; ʿalā is a preposition, and an and what is within its scope are in the position of genitive by ʿalā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to qādirin; yakhluqa has a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "huwa", and mithlahum is a direct object.
(بَلى وَهُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ): a particle of reply confirming a negation, and the wāw is a conjunction to what the affirmation conveys, that is, "Yes, He is able to do that, and He is al-Khallāq"; huwa is a mubtadaʾ, al-khallāqu the khabar, and al-ʿalīmu a second khabar. (إِنَّما أَمْرُهُ إِذا أَرادَ شَيْئاً أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): innamā: inna with the restraining mā (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); amruhu is a mubtadaʾ, idhā is an adverb of the future, the clause arāda is the genitive complement of the adverb, shayʾan is a direct object, and an and what is within its scope is the khabar of amruhu; lahu are two words attached to yaqūla, the clause kun is the content of the saying, and kun is a complete imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "anta"; the fā is a conjunction, and yakūnu is an imperfect verb in the nominative because it and its fāʿil form a clause in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is conjoined to amruhu; it was also read in the accusative, conjoined to yaqūla.
(فَسُبْحانَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): the fā is the fā al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fā), subḥāna is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and alladhī is a muḍāf ilayhi; bi-yadihi is a fronted khabar, and malakūtu kulli shayʾin is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative; wa-ilayhi: the wāw is a conjunction, and ilayhi are two words attached to turjaʿūna, and turjaʿūna is an imperfect passive verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
Excellence of exposition (ḥusn al-bayān):
In His words: «وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه» and the verses that follow, there is ḥusn al-bayān. Its reality is bringing out the meaning in the best forms that clarify it and conveying it to the understanding of the addressee by the nearest and easiest of ways. Expression of it may come by way of conciseness (ījāz) and may come by way of elaboration (iṭnāb), according to what the situation requires. The exposition of the Noble Book came in this verse by both ways, so it was comprehensive and exclusive in the decisive argument against the opponent. And it came detached from what precedes it, because He, glory be to Him, mentioned the parable (mathal), and in the whole passage, neither before nor after, there is nothing that came in the form of a parable or that could be a parable; the matter is that Umayya ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a decayed bone in his hand and said: "O Muḥammad, you claim your Lord revives this after it has come to this state?" So it was revealed. In one report it was al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and it is said that it was Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī.
The time has come to quote the eloquent passage that al-Zamakhsharī gave concerning these verses. He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, denounced their denial of the resurrection with a denunciation than which you see none more wonderful, more eloquent, or more indicative of man's persistence in disbelief, his excess in denying favours and being ungrateful for benefits, his penetration into baseness, and his deep sinking into insolence, in that He established that the substance from which he was created is the lowest and most contemptible of things, namely the foul sperm-drop that issues from the urethra, which is the channel of impurity; then He expressed wonder at his state, that one like him, with the lowliness of his origin and the meanness of his beginning, should undertake to dispute with the Almighty, turn his cheek in disputation with Him, mount the back of falsehood, persist and be obstinate, and say: 'Who is able to revive the dead after the bones have decayed?' Then his dispute is about the most inseparable and most cleaving description of himself, which is that he is brought forth from lifeless matter, while he denies his being brought forth from lifeless matter; and this is stubbornness beyond which there is no aspiration.
It is related that a group of Quraysh, among them Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī, Abū Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, spoke about that, and Ubayy said to them: 'Do you not see what Muḥammad says, that Allah resurrects the dead?' Then he said: 'By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, I will go to him and defeat him in argument.' He took a decayed bone and began to crumble it with his hand, saying: 'O Muḥammad, do you think Allah will revive this after it has decayed?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Yes, and He will resurrect you and admit you into Hell.'

dervis-irab:47-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَخِصِّمُونَ): with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the khāʾ and kasra on the doubled ṣād. Its origin is yakhtaṣimūn; when the vowel of the tāʾ was dropped it became sukūn and met the sukūn of the khāʾ, so the khāʾ was given kasra, following the principle of escaping from the meeting of two sukūns. There are other readings, to which one is referred in the longer works.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ): Conjoined to what preceded. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition; the clause (قيل) is in the position of a genitive by annexation; the clause (أنفقوا) is the content of the saying; (مما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنفقوا); and the clause (رزقكم الله) is the ṣila. (قالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: أَنُطْعِمُ مَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ): The clause (قال) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; (الذين) is the agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (للذين) is attached to (قال); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; and the hamza is for a question whose meaning is mockery. There were heretics (zanādiqa) in Mecca who, when ordered to give charity to the poor, would say, "No, by Allah! Would Allah make him poor and we feed him?"
It was also said that it was revealed about the polytheists of Quraysh, when the poor among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah said:
"Give us from your wealth that you claim belongs to Allah", meaning His saying: «وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا» ("And they assign to Allah a share of the crops and cattle He created"). So they denied them and said, "Had Allah willed, He would have fed you", in mockery of the believers, that is, "so we will not feed you until you return to our religion". (نطعم) is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (we); (من) is a direct object; (لو) is conditional; (يشاء الله) is an imperfect verb and an agent; the clause (أطعمه) has no grammatical position; and the clause (لو يشاء الله أطعمه) has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of (من).
(إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): It is either the completion of the polytheists' speech, or part of what the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said to them, or part of what Allah the Exalted said to them. Al-Qurṭubī related that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, used to feed the poor Muslims, and Abū Jahl met him and said: "O Abū Bakr, do you claim that Allah is able to feed these people?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then why does He not feed them?" He said: "He has tried some people with poverty and others with wealth, and has commanded the poor to be patient and the rich to give." Abū Jahl said: "By Allah, O Abū Bakr, you are only in error! Do you claim that Allah is able to feed these people and yet He does not feed them, and then you feed them?" So the verse was revealed. (وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): A resumptive speech to explain another kind of their perversity and their riding the back of error. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (متى) is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverbial, and the adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (هذا) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الوعد) is a badal from the demonstrative; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم صادقين) is (كان) with its noun and khabar; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is, "so when is this promise?"
(ما يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ): (ما) is negative; (ينظرون) is an imperfect verb and an agent, and its meaning is "they await": He made them awaiting its occurrence although they were certain that it would not happen, in imitation of their speech. (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (صيحة) is a direct object; (واحدة) is an adjective; the clause (تأخذهم) is a second adjective or a ḥāl clause; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; (هم) is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يخصمون) is the khabar; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning is that it will seize them suddenly while they are deep in heedlessness, giving themselves up to disputes about trade and dealings. (فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً وَلا إِلى أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (يستطيعون) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (توصية) is a direct object; the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (إلى أهلهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يرجعون); and the clause is conjoined to (فلا يستطيعون).

dervis-irab:51-54.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصُّورِ): It is the horn, or what is called today the būq (trumpet), a hollow elongated thing that is blown into and played, and its plural is abwāq, bīqān and būqāt.
Abū al-Fatḥ ibn Jinnī said: Someone with no experience of the speech of the Arabs faulted Abū al-Ṭayyib for pluralising būq as būqāt in his saying:
إذا كان بعض الناس سيفا لدولة ... ففي الناس بوقات لها وطبول
(If some men are a sword for a dynasty, then among men there are trumpets and drums for it.)
Analogy supports it, since it has many parallels, such as ḥamām and ḥamāmāt, surādiq and surādiqāt, and jawāb and jawābāt; it is frequent in all masculine nouns for non-rational things.
(الْأَجْداثِ): the graves, plural of jadath, like faras and afrās. It was also read min al-ajdāf with fāʾ, which is a dialectal variant of al-ajdāth; one says jadath and jadaf.
(يَنْسِلُونَ): "they run", with kasra or ḍamma on the sīn. One says nasala al-dhiʾb yansilu, of the pattern ḍaraba yaḍribu, and it was said that yansulu with ḍamma also occurs; it is hurrying in walking. In al-Qāmūs: "nasala yansilu and yansulu, with kasra or ḍamma on the sīn, naslan, nasalan and nasalānan: he hurried in his walk."
From it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فإن تك ساءتك مني خليقة ... فسلّي ثيابي من ثيابك تنسل
(If some trait of mine has displeased you, then pull my clothes from your clothes and they will slip away.)

* I'rab:
(وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَإِذا هُمْ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ إِلى رَبِّهِمْ يَنْسِلُونَ): A resumptive speech, delivered to establish the resurrection on the Day of Judgement. (نفخ) is a passive past verb, the deputy agent being latent, its implied form being "huwa" (he); (في الصور) is attached to (نفخ); the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا) is the particle of surprise; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (من الأجداث) is attached to (ينسلون); (إلى ربهم) is also attached to (ينسلون); and the clause (ينسلون) is their khabar. (قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا مَنْ بَعَثَنا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنا): (قالوا) is a verb and an agent; (يا) is a particle of alerting or a vocative particle and the one addressed is omitted; (ويلنا) is a maṣdar with no verb of its own wording, and (نا) is a muḍāf ilayhi. It is permissible that it be an annexed vocative, of the figurative vocative, that is, "O woe, be present, for this is your time". (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ; the clause (بعثنا) is the khabar; and (من مرقدنا) is attached to (بعثنا). For (المرقد) it is permissible that it be a maṣdar mīmī (a verbal noun with initial mīm), that is, "from our sleep", and permissible that it be a noun of place, the singular having been put in the place of the plural. (هذا ما وَعَدَ الرَّحْمنُ وَصَدَقَ الْمُرْسَلُونَ): (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (ما) is a relative noun, the khabar; the clause (وعد الرحمن) is a verb and an agent, and the object of (وعد) is omitted, that is, "wa'adanā" (promised us); (وصدق المرسلون) is a verb and an agent, the object being omitted. On this i'rab the pause at (مرقدنا) is complete. It is permissible that (ما) be a maṣdar, and it with what follows it would be the khabar of (هذا). Al-Zamakhsharī and others permitted that the demonstrative be an adjective of (مرقدنا), so that one pauses at it, and (ما وعد) would be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the implied form on the first is "ḥaqq" (true) and on the second "hādhā" (this) or "baʿthunā" (our resurrection).
(إِنْ كانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَإِذا هُمْ جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ): (إن) is negative; (كانت) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "al-ṣayḥa" (the cry); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (صيحة) is the khabar of (كانت); the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا) is the particle of surprise; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (جميع) is a khabar; (لدينا) is an adverb attached to (محضرون); and (محضرون) is a second khabar or an adjective of (جميع). (فَالْيَوْمَ لا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئاً وَلا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): The fāʾ is resumptive; (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (تظلم); (لا) is negative; (تظلم) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the deputy agent [Translator's note: this is as written in the source; the deputy agent of (تظلم) is in fact (نفس), and the wāw belongs to (تجزون)]; (ولا تجزون) is conjoined to (لا تظلم) by way of iltifāt; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (ما) is the second direct object of (تجزون); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا» there is an explicit primary metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya aṣliyya). He borrowed sleep (al-ruqād) for death, the common ground between them being the absence of appearance of action, since neither the sleeper nor the dead shows any action, the intended action being deliberate, significant action, so it is not an objection that the sleeper produces some action. We said it is primary because (المرقد) is a maṣdar mīmī, as already stated; but if we make it a noun of place, the metaphor is a derivative one (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya).

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَكِيمِ): the possessor of wisdom (ḥikma). One says "a wise poem (qaṣīda ḥakīma)", i.e. one possessing wisdom. Wisdom has been discussed before. Ḥakuma al-rajul, of the pattern karuma, means the man became wise. From it is the saying of al-Nābigha:
واحكم كحكم فتاة الحي إذ نظرت ... إلى حمام شراع وارد الثمد
(Judge like the judgement of the girl of the tribe when she looked at a flock of doves, swift, coming to the shallow water.)
"Experiences made him wise (aḥkamathu al-tajārib)" means they made him wise. Another said:
وقصيدة تأتي الملوك حكيمة ... قد قلتها ليقال من ذا قالها
(And a wise poem that comes to kings; I composed it so that it would be asked, "Who said it?")
The wording of al-Karkhī: "faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, like their saying 'I thickened the honey (ʿaqadtu), so it is ʿaqīd' in the sense of muʿqad (thickened); it is not in the sense of mafʿūl, as in 'an accursed devil (shayṭān rajīm)', meaning marjūm (stoned), and it is not so in the verse, because one would then say 'ruled by it (maḥkūm bihi)' and the like; nor in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. ruler (ḥākim), because the true Ruler is Allah the Exalted. So it is clear thereby that the Wise Qur'an is 'ruled in' (maḥkūm fīhi) not 'ruler', and that the absolute Ruler is Allah the Exalted; or it is in the sense of attribution (nisba), i.e. possessor of wisdom, because it is a speaking proof of wisdom, by way of metaphor, and the one described by it by way of figurative attribution."
(الْأَذْقانِ): plural of dhaqan, with fatḥa on the dhāl and qāf, and with kasra on the dhāl and fatḥa on the qāf: the place where the two jaws meet, at their bottom.
(مُقْمَحُونَ): al-muqmaḥ is he who raises his head and lowers his gaze. One says qamaḥa al-baʿīr, so he is qāmiḥ, when it raises its head after drinking, from having quenched its thirst, or from the coldness of the water, or from dislike of its taste. In al-Mukhtār: "Al-iqmāḥ: raising the head and lowering the gaze. One says 'the iron collar made him raise his head (aqmaḥahu al-ghull)' when it leaves his head raised because of its tightness." And in al-Qāmūs: "The collar made the captive raise his head (aqmaḥa al-ghull al-asīr): it left his head raised because of its tightness."
(سَدًّا): al-sadd and al-saddd, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the sīn: the barrier between two things, and the mountain; the plural is asdād. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: «وضرب على قلبه بالأسداد» (and his heart was struck with barriers), i.e. the roads were blocked to him and the paths were blinded for him. [Translator's note: the source prints "al-sadd and al-sadd" with the two forms distinguished only by vowelling, which is lost in the unvowelled text; the two forms are sadd (fatḥa) and sudd (ḍamma).]
(فَأَغْشَيْناهُمْ): i.e. "We covered their eyes (abṣārahum)", that is, We veiled them and put over them a covering so that they cannot aspire to anything seen. More of these images will come in the sections on Rhetoric and I'rab.

* I'rab:
(يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ): (يس): the discussion of the openings of the sūras, in meaning and parsing, has already been given. The wāw is a particle of oath and of genitive; (القرآن) is the thing sworn by; (الحكيم) is an adjective; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element whose implied form is "I swear (uqsimu)".
(إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): (إن) and its subject (ism); the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (من المرسلين) is its khabar (predicate).
(عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): (على صراط) is a second khabar of (إن), and it is said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be attached to (المرسلين), (مستقيم) being an adjective of (صراط), i.e. "those who were sent on a straight way", and there is no harm in this parsing.
(تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ): (تنزيل) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "the Qur'an was sent down (nuzzila) as a sending down", and it is annexed to its agent; or it is accusative by an omitted verb whose implied form is "I mean" or "I praise". It was read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "«تنزيل العزيز الرحيم» was read in the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, in the accusative on 'I mean', and in the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «القرآن»."
(لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْماً ما أُنْذِرَ آباؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غافِلُونَ): the lām is for justification; (تنذر) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of justification; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تنزيل) or to the meaning of His saying (من المرسلين), i.e. "sent in order that you warn"; (قوما) is a direct object; (ما) is negative, because no prophet was sent to Quraysh before Muḥammad ﷺ; (أنذر) is a passive past verb and (آباؤهم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); on this, the sentence is an adjective of (قوما), i.e. a people who were not warned. It is also permissible that (ما) be relative, or an indefinite with an adjective, or a maṣdar particle, in which case it is parsed, with its adjective or ṣila or maṣdar, as a second object of (تنذر) on the first two views and as an absolute object on the third. We shall present the three interpretations to you:
The relative: "that you warn a people of that of which their fathers were warned."
The indefinite: "that you warn a people of a punishment of which their fathers were warned."
The maṣdar: "that you warn a people with the warning of their fathers."
The redundant: Abū al-Baqāʾ gave a fourth view, that it is redundant (zāʾida) and the clause (أنذر) is an adjective of (قوما).
(فهم): the fāʾ is a fāʾ of justification for the negation if (ما) is made negative, i.e. "they were not warned, so they are heedless", on the basis that their not being warned is the cause of their heedlessness; or it is a justification for the sending, as you say, "I sent you to so-and-so to warn him, for he is heedless". (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (غافلون) is a khabar.
(لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلى أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of confirmation; (حق القول) is a verb and an agent; (على أكثرهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حق); the fāʾ is also for justification; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the khabar. The meaning is: "By Allah, the Word has been established and has come true against them because of their persistence in disbelief and denial."
(إِنَّا جَعَلْنا فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقانِ فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ): a resumptive speech conveyed to give a parable of their determination on disbelief, and that there is no way to their turning back from their error. (إن) and its subject; the clause (جعلنا) is its khabar; (جعلنا) is a verb and an agent; (في أعناقهم) is in the position of an accusative as the second object of (جعلنا); (أغلالا) is the first object of (جعلنا); (فهي): the fāʾ is for conjunction with immediate sequence, or for conjunction with justification (the difference between the two meanings will come); (هي) is a mubtadaʾ; (الى الأذقان) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar, i.e. "gathered" or "raised". More of the secrets of this expression will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فهم): the fāʾ is like the first fāʾ, and some called it the fāʾ of consequence; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (مقمحون) is a khabar.
(وَجَعَلْنا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا): the wāw is a conjunction; (جعلنا) is a verb and an agent; (من بين أيديهم) is in the position of an accusative as the second object of (جعلنا); (سدا) is the first object of (جعلنا); (ومن خلفهم سدا) is conjoined to (من بين أيديهم سدا).
(فَأَغْشَيْناهُمْ فَهُمْ لا يُبْصِرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أغشيناهم) is a verb, an agent and a direct object; the fāʾ is for justification; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يبصرون) is the khabar of (هم).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا» the verse contains various arts, which we present below:
1 - The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
Much has been said of the istiʿāra tamthīliyya. It is here a parable of their determination on disbelief and their persistence in obstinacy, in that He made them like those who are shackled and made to raise their heads, who do not turn to the truth and do not bend their necks toward it, because the collars reach the chins and are fastened to them, so they do not let them bow; so they are always raised-headed (muqmaḥūn), lifting their heads and lowering their gaze. That is, their condition and form, in the faith not being made available to them, was likened to the form of one whose hand and neck were shackled so that he cannot take what they want; and the common ground is absolute obstruction. An important question remains: does the pronoun in His saying (فهي إلى الأذقان) refer to the collars or to the hands? Al-Zamakhsharī preferred its return to the collars. He said: "So the collars reach the chins and are fastened to them, and that is because the ring of the collar on the neck of the shackled man has its two ends meeting under the chin in a ring in which is the head of the pillar standing out from the ring to the chin, so it does not let him bow his head and lower his nape, and he is ever raised-headed." Al-Zamakhsharī went on to support his view of the pronoun's return to the collars, saying: "If you say, what do you say about the one who makes the pronoun refer to the hands, and claims that since the collar gathers the hand and the neck, and for that is called a jāmiʿa, the mention of the necks indicates the mention of the hands? I say: the right view is what I have mentioned to you, and the evidence for it is His saying: «فهم مقمحون». Do you not see how He made the raising of the head the result of His saying «فهي إلى الأذقان»? Had the pronoun referred to the hands, the sense of causation in the raising of the head would not be apparent; besides, this implied reading contains a kind of arbitrariness and the leaving of the apparent sense which the meaning itself calls for, for a falsehood which it rejects, and the leaving of the clear truth for tangled falsehood." Perhaps al-Zamakhsharī reached the summit in this unique exposition and showed his familiarity with and mastery of the science of bayān; yet the second view, the return of the pronoun to the hands, is not without merit and loftiness of expression, and in it is exaggeration in depicting the terror, which fits the flow of the speech: for although the hand is not mentioned in the wording, the collar indicates it and even requires it, and there is no doubt that pressing the hand together with the neck on the neck necessitates the raising of the head. Add to this that when the hand is loosed and free, the shackled man has some joy in its freedom, and perhaps he uses it for contrivance and help in undoing the collar, which is not so when it is shackled. So there is added to the dispersed similitudes that preceded that the closing of the door of contrivance against them in guidance and in slipping out of the noose of disbelief decreed for them is likened to the shackling of the hands, because the hand, as we have said, is the tool of contrivance and the means to deliverance.
2 - A second representational metaphor:
In His saying «وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا الآية» is a second istiʿāra tamthīliyya. He likened them to those who are surrounded by two terrible barriers which covered their eyes so that they see neither before nor behind them, in that they are imprisoned in the pit of ignorance, barred from looking at the signs and proofs; or as if, having been deprived of the blessing of reflection upon past ages and bygone nations and of contemplation of coming outcomes and future ends, they were enclosed by a barrier in front of them and a barrier behind them, so they are in a dark gloom in which the eye does not catch from its side a spark, nor discern a gleam of hope.
3 - Inversion (al-qalb):
In His saying «إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا» is inversion, which is one of the arts of Arab speech, since the reality is "We put their necks in the collars". Thaʿlab said, regarding His saying, the Exalted: «ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه», that the meaning is "insert a chain into it", i.e. "put a chain into his neck". [Translator's note: the source attributes to Thaʿlab a reading of the verse as "insert a chain into it"; it is translated as written.]
4 - Indefiniteness (al-tankīr):
In the indefiniteness of (أغلالا) is exaggeration in magnifying them and making their matter terrible.

dervis-irab:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(وَسَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): a resumptive speech (kalām mustaʾnaf) conveyed to explain their state by way of rebuke after explaining it by way of parable; you may also conjoin it to what precedes, in which case the wāw is a conjunction. (سواء) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سواء); the hamza is for interrogation, and it is the hamza of equalization (hamzat al-taswiya), whose discussion has been given in detail in Sūrat al-Baqara, so it is as there. It and the verb after it are, in interpretation, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "equal in your view is your warning them and your not warning them". (أم) is a conjunction equivalent to the hamza; (لم) is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; (تنذرهم) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم), its agent latent, and the hāʾ a direct object. The clause (لا يؤمنون) is a resumption (istiʾnāf) that confirms what precedes, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) that confirms it, or a badal (substitute) from it.
(إِنَّما تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ): (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa (restrictive); (تنذر) is an imperfect verb and its agent is latent, the implied form being "you"; (من) is a direct object; the clause (اتبع الذكر) is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (خشي الرحمن) is conjoined to (اتبع الذكر); (بالغيب) is a ḥāl from the agent or from the direct object. We ask: what is the reason for mentioning the second warning in a manner opposing the first, when the first is affirmative? The reason is that the aim sought by the warning, which is faith, is not attained, so He followed with «إنما تنذر», in the sense that the aim is attained only by your warning of people other than these warned ones, namely those who followed the Reminder, which is the Qur'an, and those who fear their Lord; so what is restricted is only the beneficial warning, and the existence of other warning, for those who do not benefit from it, does not contradict it.
(فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); (بشره) is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; (بمغفرة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بشره); (أجر) is conjoined to (بمغفرة); (كريم) is an adjective of (أجر).
(إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَنَكْتُبُ ما قَدَّمُوا وَآثارَهُمْ): (إن) and its subject; (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); the clause (نحيي الموتى) is the khabar of (نحن) and the sentence is the khabar of (إن), or the sentence is the khabar of (إنا); (ونكتب) is conjoined to (نحيي); (ما) is a direct object and the clause (قدموا) is the ṣila of (ما); (وآثارهم) is conjoined to (ما), and what is meant by it is what they instituted that was followed after them. In the Ḥadīth: "Whoever institutes a good practice and it is acted upon after him, will have its reward and the like of the reward of whoever acts upon it, without anything being diminished from their rewards; and whoever institutes an evil practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it after him, without anything being diminished from their burden."
(وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ فِي إِمامٍ مُبِينٍ): (كل شيء) is accusative by an omitted verb that is explained by what follows it, so it is accusative by occupation (ishtighāl); (أحصيناه) is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the sentence is explicative and has no grammatical position; (في إمام) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أحصيناه); (مبين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (إمام), i.e. "in a clear book".

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿يسۤ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: a shaykh of the people of Kufa narrated to me from al-Ḥasan himself, who said: Yā Sīn: "O man." In Arabic it is equivalent to a letter of the alphabet, as in your saying ﴿حم﴾ and the like.
The reading is with the nūn of يس quiescent (in pause). I have heard some Arabs give it a fatḥa and say ﴿ياسينَ والقرآنِ الحكِيم﴾, as though making it vowelled in the way particles are vowelled when what precedes [the last letter] is quiescent; like لَيْتَ and لعلّ, of which the last letter takes a fatḥa when the letter next to it is quiescent. And had it been given a kasra, as جَيْرِ is given a kasra in جَيْرِ لا أفعلُ ذلكَ ("indeed, I will not do that") — it was given a kasra because of the yāʾ in جَيْرِ. [Translator's note: the source does not complete the conditional.]

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ may be a predicate after a predicate [Translator's note: the source has خيراً, apparently for خبراً, "predicate"]: "you are surely among the messengers; you are on a straight path." It may also be: you are surely among those who were sent on a straight path, on uprightness.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿تَنزِيلَ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾: the reading is in the accusative, on [the analogy of] your saying: truly, you are among the messengers, as a revelation, truly. The people of the Ḥijāz read it in the nominative, while ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it in the accusative. Whoever makes it nominative makes it a third predicate: you are surely the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful. Its nominative may also be as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), as in your saying: "that is the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful"; as He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلاَّ سَاعةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. that is a proclamation.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ﴾: it is said: that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, i.e. you did not warn them, nor did any messenger come to them before you. It is also said: that you may warn them with what their fathers were warned with; then the bāʾ is dropped, so (ما) is in the position of an accusative; as He said ﴿أنْذَرْتكُم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صَاعِقَةِ عَادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِيۤ أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلاَلاً فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلأَذْقَانِ﴾: He used the pronoun هى ("they"), which refers to the right hands, though they were not mentioned. That is because a shackle (ghull) is only on the right hand and the neck, joining the right hand and the neck, so mention of one of them suffices for the other; as He said ﴿فمنْ خَافَ مِنْ مُوصٍ جَنَفاً أو إثماً فأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, joining the heirs with the testator though they were not mentioned, because reconciliation takes place only between the testator and the heirs. Similar is the poet's saying:
وما أدرى إذا يمّمت وجهاً * أُريد الخير أيُّهما يلينى
أَأَلخير الذى أَنَا أبتغيه * أم الشرّ الذى لا يأتلينى
(I do not know, when I head in some direction seeking good, which of the two will come to me: the good that I seek, or the evil that does not fail to seek me.)
He used a pronoun for the evil though he had mentioned only the good, because evil is mentioned together with good. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (إنا جعنا فى أَيْمانهم أغلالاً فهى إلى الأذقان} ("We have put shackles on their right hands") [Translator's note: جعنا in the source quotation is apparently for جعلنا]. So "right hands" sufficed for mention of the necks in ʿAbd Allāh's text, and "necks" sufficed for "right hands" in the reading of the general readership. Al-dhaqan is the lowest part of the two jawbones. Al-muqmaḥ is one who lowers his gaze after raising his head. Its meaning is: We have held them back from spending in the way of Allah.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَأغْشَيْنَاهُمْ﴾, i.e. We covered their eyes with a covering. This verse was revealed concerning a group of the Banū Makhzūm who wanted to kill the Prophet ﷺ. They came to him at his place of prayer by night, and Allah blinded their eyes to him, so they could hear his voice reciting the Qurʾān but could not see him. That is His saying ﴿فَأغْشَيْنَاهُمْ﴾. It is also read ﴿فأعْشَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ with ʿayn: We made them night-blind to him; because al-ʿashw is at night: when evening comes and you cannot see anything, that is al-ʿashw.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَكْتُبُ مَاَ قَدَّمُواْ﴾: as for "what they sent ahead", it is the deeds they did beforehand; and "their traces" are the practices followed after them. It is / 156 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] like His saying ﴿يُنَبَّأُ الإنْسانُ يَوْمَئذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأخَّرَ﴾.
His saying ﴿وَكُلَّ شيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِيۤ إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: the readers agree on the accusative of (كُلّ), because the verb falls on the pronoun referring back to it. The nominative is a good form; I have heard it from the Arabs; because (كُلّ) is like an indefinite noun when accompanied by negation. The Arabs say هل أحد ضربته (is there anyone you struck?), and (كلّ) carries the same interpretation; do you not see that its meaning is: there is nothing but that We have counted it?

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿إِلَيْهِمُ ٱثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ﴾: the third had been sent before the two, and was called a liar, while you see it in the revelation as though it were after them. The meaning of His saying ﴿فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ﴾ is only: with the third who was before them; as if you said: then We reinforced with the first. As for the reinforcing, He says: We strengthened their cause through what the first, Shamʿūn (Simon), taught them. They had been sent to Antioch. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (فعَزَّزنا بالثالث) ("with the third"), because he had [already] been mentioned among the messengers [Translator's note: ذركر in the source is apparently for ذُكر]; and when an indefinite noun is mentioned in something and then repeated, it comes out definite; as when you say to a man: "I have given you two dirhams," and he says: "So where are the two dirhams (al-dirhamān)?" ʿĀṣim read (فعَزَزْنا) light [without doubling]; it is like your saying شدّدنا and شدَدنا.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾: He means: we will kill you. Most of what occurs in the Qurʾān of stoning (rajm) is killing; like His saying ﴿وَلَوْلاَ رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْنَاكَ﴾.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿طَائِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ﴾: the readers agree on (طائركم) with alif. The Arabs [also] say طيركم معكم.
His saying: ﴿أَئِِن ذُكِّرْتُم﴾: the reading of the general readership is with hamza and kasra on the alif of (إنْ).
Abū Razīn — who was one of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh — read ﴿أََأَنْ ذُكِّرتم﴾. Whoever gives it kasra, saying ﴿أَئِن﴾, makes it a conditional (jazāʾ) on which the interrogative alif has entered. It is reported of some readers: (طائركم معكم أين ذُكِّرْتم) and ﴿ذُكِرتم﴾, meaning: your omen is with you wherever you are. Al-ṭāʾir here means deeds and provision; He says: it is on your necks. Whoever makes it ﴿أَين﴾ should make ﴿ذكرتم﴾ light; Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī made ﴿ذُكرتم﴾ light, but I do not have (أين) memorised from him.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ آمَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ﴾, i.e. bear witness to that for me. Ḥabīb says it to the three messengers.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي﴾: (بمَا) may be in the position of (الذى) [i.e. a relative noun], or (ما) with (غفر) may be in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had you made (مَا) in the sense of (أىّ), it would have been correct; the meaning would be: would that they knew for what thing my Lord forgave me. Had it been so, it would have been permissible for it to be ﴿بِمَ غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي﴾ with the alif dropped; as you say: سَلْ عَمَّ شئت (ask about whatever you wish), and as He said ﴿فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ المُرْسَلُون﴾. The poet kept it complete while it was interrogative, saying:
إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سَرَاتَكُمُ * أهلَ اللواء ففِيما يُكثَر القِيل
(We have killed, for our slain, your chiefs, the bearers of the banner; so over what is there so much talk?)

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: the readers put it in the accusative, except Abū Jaʿfar, who put it in the nominative, on the basis of not implying a noun in (كانت). The accusative is when you imply [a noun] in it; as you say: "Go, for there is none but Allah, the One, the Subduer" — الواحدُ القهّارُ and الواحدَ القهَّار — on this interpretation. I heard one of the Arabs say of a man whom he was describing as cunning: لو لم يكن إلاّ ظِلُّه لخَابَّ ظِلُّه (if there were nothing but his shadow, his shadow would play the cheat). The nominative and the accusative are both permissible. The readers have read (إلاّ أنْ تكونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً) in the nominative and the accusative, and this is of that kind.
His saying: ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿إنْ كانَتْ إلاَّ زَقْيَةً﴾ ("but a single cry"). Zaqya and zaqwa are two dialectal forms; one says zaqaytu and zaqawtu. One of them recited to me, mentioning a woman:
تلد غلاماً عَارماً يؤذيكِ * ولو زَقَوت كَزُقاء الدّيك
(She will bear a wild boy who will hurt you, even if you cry out like the crowing of a cock.)

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰحَسْرَةً عَلَى ٱلْعِبَادِ﴾: the meaning is: O what a regret over the servants! Some read ﴿يا حسرةَ العباد﴾, and the meaning in Arabic is the same, and Allah knows best. When the Arabs call an indefinite noun connected with something [following it], they prefer the accusative; they say: يا رَجلا كريماً أَقبِل (O noble man, come forward) and يا راكباً على البعير أَقبل (O rider on the camel, come forward). When they make it single, they use the nominative more / 156 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] than the accusative. One of them recited to me:
يا سيّدا ما أنت من سَيّدٍ * موطّأ الأعقابِ رَحْبَ الذراع
قوَّال معروف وفعّاله * نحّار أُمَّات الرِّباع الرِّتَاع
(O lord — what a lord you are! — with a well-trodden threshold, broad of arm, speaker of kindness and doer of it, slaughterer of the mothers of the grazing young camels.)
One of the Banū Sulaym recited it to me with (موطّأ) in the nominative, and al-Kisāʾī recited it to me with (موطأ) in the genitive. Another recited to me:
ألا يَا قتيلاً ما قتيلَ بنى حِلْس * إذا ابتلَّ أطرافُ الرماح من الدّعْسِ
(O slain man — what a slain man of the Banū Ḥils! — when the tips of the spears are wet from thrusting.)
Had you put the indefinite noun connected with the adjective in the nominative, it would have been correct. The Arabs have said:
* يا دار غيّرها البلى تغييرا *
(O abode, which decay has changed utterly.)
meaning: O you abode which [decay] has changed. I heard Abū al-Jarrāḥ say to a man: أَيا مَجْنُونُ مَجْنُونُ (O madman, madman), by way of following. And I heard from the Arabs: يا مهتمُّ بأمرنا لا تهتمّ (O you who are concerned about our affair, do not be concerned), meaning: O you who are concerned.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا﴾: (كَمْ) is in the position of an accusative on two grounds. One is that you make ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ fall on ﴿كَمْ﴾; in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ألم يروا مَن أهلكنا) ("have they not seen whom We destroyed?"); that is one way. The other is that you make ﴿اهلكنا﴾ fall on (كم) and make it interrogative; as you say: علمت كم ضربتَ غلامك (I know how many times you struck your slave). When رَأيْت and what is derived from it, or knowing and what is derived from it, and whatever resembles them in meaning, precede مَن, أىّ and كم, it is permissible to make what comes after كم, أىّ, من and the like fall on them; as Allah said ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَىُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصَى﴾: do you not see that you have cancelled the knowing from falling on أىّ, and made أيّ nominative by أحصى? In the same way you make it accusative by a verb, if [the verb] falls on it.
His saying ﴿أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾: its alif is given fatḥa, because the meaning is: have they not seen that they will not return to them? Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī gave it kasra, as though he did not make the seeing fall on (كم), and so did not make it fall on (أنّ). If you wish, you give it kasra as a fresh start, and make كم accusative by يروا falling on it.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ﴾: al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim doubled it. Many people made it light, among them readers of the people of Medina, and it has reached me that ʿAlī made it light. That is the proper form, because it is (ما) on which a lām has been put that serves as the answer to إنْ; as though you said: and all of them are surely gathered, brought before Us. But those who made it heavy did so only on a correct basis. If you wish, you may mean: وإن كل لِمَن ما جميع, and then one of the mīms was elided because there were so many of them, as [the poet] said:
غداة طفَتْ عَلْماءِ بكرُ بن وائل * وعُجْنَا صدورَ الخيل نحوَ تميم
(On the morning when Bakr ibn Wāʾil floated on the water [ʿalā al-māʾ], and we turned the horses' chests towards Tamīm.)
The other way of [explaining] the doubling is that they make (لَمَّا) equivalent to (إلاَّ) with (إنْ) specifically; it is then in its manner like إنما when it is put in the sense of إلاَّ: as though it were لَمْ to which مَا was joined, and the two together became (an exception, and left the domain of negation. We consider that the Arabs' word (إلاَّ) is only that they combined the إن that is negative and joined (لا) to it, so the two together became one particle and left the domain of negation when they were combined and became one particle. Likewise لمّا. Similar to that is His saying ﴿لولا﴾: it is only لو to which لا was joined, so they became one particle. Al-Kisāʾī used to reject this view, and say: I do not know any way for لَمّا with doubling in the reading. [Translator's note: the parenthesis opened before "an exception" is not closed in the source.]

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿لِيَأْكُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ), and all are correct. The Arabs leave the hāʾ implicit with الذى, مَن and مَا, and make it overt; all of that is correct. ﴿وَمَا عَمِلَتْ﴾: (ما), if you wish, is in the position of a genitive: that they may eat of its fruit and of what their hands have made. If you wish, you make it a negation and give it no grammatical position; the meaning is then: We made for them gardens, palms and vines, and their hands did not make it; ﴿أَفَلاَ يَشْكُرُونَ﴾.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ﴾: if someone says: what is His saying ﴿نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ﴾? Its meaning is only: We strip the day from it: We cast the day off from it, and darkness comes. Likewise the night is stripped from the day, and light comes. This is well-known Arabic; do you not see His saying ﴿آتَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا فَانْسَلَخَ مِنْهَا﴾, i.e. he went out of them and left them? Likewise the night and the day.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَـا﴾: to the measure of its courses: the fixed measure. Whoever says ﴿لا مستقرّ لهَا﴾ or ﴿لا مُسْتَقَرٌّ لها﴾ ("there is no resting-place for it") — these are two good forms, making it always running. As for putting المستقرّ in the genitive [after لا], I do not know what that is.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾: the nominative in it pleases me more than the accusative, because He said ﴿وآيةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ﴾ and then made the sun and the moon follow the night, and in its manner they are signs like it. Whoever makes it accusative means: and We measured the moon in stations, as We did with the sun; so he refers it back to the hāʾ of the sun in meaning, not that he makes fall on it what fell on the sun. Similar in ordinary speech: عبدالله يقوم وجَاريتَه يضربها (ʿAbd Allāh stands, and his slave-girl he beats): the slave-girl is referred back to the verb, not to the noun; for that reason we make it accusative, because the wāw in it belongs to the later verb.
His saying: ﴿كَٱلعُرجُونِ﴾: al-ʿurjūn is what lies between the date-stalks (shamārīkh) and the part growing on the palm. "Old" (al-qadīm) in this place is that over which a year has passed.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِي لَهَآ أَن تدْرِكَ ٱلقَمَرَ﴾: He says: [it does not befit the sun to] rise at night, nor for the night to outstrip the day; He says: nor is it for the moon to rise by day, i.e. it would have no light. It is also said: it does not befit the sun to overtake the moon and take away its light, nor for the night to outstrip the day and darken it. The position of ﴿أَن تدْرِكَ﴾ is nominative.

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾: He is addressing only the people of Mecca, and He made the offspring that were with Noah belong to the people of Mecca, because they are their origin; so He said ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ — they are the children of that offspring.

farraa:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِّن مِّثْلِهِ﴾: of the like of Noah's ark; ﴿مَا يَرْكَبُونَ﴾: He says: We made for them ships fashioned on that model; these are the skiffs and the like in which people ride. If a reader were to read من مَثَلَه it would be a valid form, meaning "of its model": I have heard of anyone reading it so. [Translator's note: so in the source; a negation (لم) appears to have dropped out, i.e. "I have not heard of anyone reading it so".]

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ﴾: al-ṣarīkh is rescue.

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا﴾: He says: except that We do that as a mercy. His saying ﴿وَمَتَاعاً إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾: He says: survival until a term, i.e. We have mercy on them and give them enjoyment for a time.

farraa:45-46.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱتَّقُواْ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾: of the punishment of the Hereafter; ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾: of the punishment of this world, which you are not safe from, of the punishment of Thamūd and those who have passed.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ كَانُواْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ is the answer to [the mention of] the sign, and the answer to His saying ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُواْ﴾. Since they turned away from every sign, the answer to one sufficed for the two, because the meaning is: when it is said to them, "Fear," they turn away; and when a sign comes to them, they turn away.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it (يخْصِمُونَ), and ʿĀṣim read it (يَخِصَّمُون), with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the khāʾ. A fatḥa on the khāʾ is also permissible, because the tāʾ [of يختصمون] used to have a fatḥa, and its vowel was transferred to the khāʾ; but the kasra is more common and better. The people of the Ḥijāz read it ﴿يَخْصّمونَ﴾, doubling [the ṣād] and combining two quiescent letters. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is (يَخْتَصِمونَ), and this is an argument for those who double. As for the meaning of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb['s reading], it may be in the sense of yafʿalūna from al-khuṣūma (disputing), as though He said: while they are talking. It may also be in another way: وهم يخصمونَ — while they, in their own minds, are defeating in argument those who promised them the Hour. That is a good interpretation, i.e. the Hour seizes them; because the meaning is: while they, in their own estimation, are overcoming whoever told them that the Hour is coming.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً﴾: He says: none of them / 157 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] is able to give a last instruction to another. ﴿وَلاَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾, i.e. they do not return a word to their families. It is also said: لا يرجعون: they are not able to return to their families from the markets.

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿مَن بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا﴾: it is said that the speech ends at المرقد. Then the angels said to them: ﴿هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمـٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾; so (هذا) and (ما) are in the position of a nominative, as though you said: this is the promise of the Most Merciful. It may also be ﴿مَن بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا هَذَا﴾, so that (هذا) is a naʿt (adjective) of المرقد, in the genitive, and (مَا) is in the position of a nominative: the promise of the Most Merciful has raised you. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿مَنْ أَهَبَّنا من مرقدنا هَذا﴾ ("who has roused us from this sleeping-place of ours?"). Al-baʿth in this place is like waking up; you say بعثت ناقتى فانبعثت (I roused my she-camel and she rose) when he stirred her up.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿فَاكِهُونَ﴾: with alif. It is also read ﴿فكِهونَ﴾, and it is like ḥadhirūn and ḥādhirūn. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (فاكهينَ) with alif.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَى ٱلأَرَآئِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾, and [also] ﴿عَلى الأرائك متكِئينَ﴾, accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment) [i.e. as ḥāl (circumstantial)]. In our reading it is nominative, because it is the end of the predicate.
His saying ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍٍ﴾: He meant the plural of ẓulla: ẓulal. It may also be ﴿ظِلاَلاً﴾, which is a plural of ẓulla, as you say ḥulla and ḥulal, and when they are many, ḥilāl; and [likewise] jilāl and qilāl. Whoever says ﴿فِي ظِلاَلٍ﴾, it is the plural of ẓill (shade). [Translator's note: the source has خُلَّة, apparently for حُلَّة, in the example.]

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿سَلاَمٌ قَوْلاً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿سَلاَماً قوْلاً﴾. Whoever puts it in the nominative says: that is theirs: "Peace," as a word; i.e. what they call for is theirs, handed over, pure, i.e. it is purely theirs; he makes it a predicate for His saying ﴿لَهُمْ مَا يَدَّعُونَ﴾: pure. It is [also] made nominative as a fresh start, meaning: that is theirs: peace. And the accusative of القول, if you wish, is on the basis that it issues from السلام, as though you said: He said it as a word. If you wish, you make it accusative from His saying ﴿لهم ما يدعون﴾ [as a word], as in your saying: a promise from Allah.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ولِتُكَلّمنَا) ("and so that [their hands] may speak to Us"), as though He said: We seal their mouths so that [their hands] may speak to Us. The wāw in this place is like His saying ﴿وَكَذِلِكَ نُرِى إبراهيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَمَواتِ والأَرْضِ وَلِيَكُون﴾.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿نُنَكِّـسْهُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ﴾: ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (ننكِّسْه) with doubling, and al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read (نَنْكُسْهُ) light, with fatḥa on the nūn.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ﴾: the readers agree on fatḥa on the rāʾ, because the meaning is: and of them is what they ride. That is strengthened by ʿĀʾisha having read (فَمِنْها رَكُوبَتُهم). If a reader were to read (فمنها رُكوبهم) ("of them is their riding"), as you say: of them is their eating, their drinking and their riding, it would be a valid form.

farraa:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلأَخْضَرِ﴾: He did not say الخُضْر (plural). And Allah has said ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ﴾ and did not say أخضر (singular). Rafraf is masculine, like shajar; but shajar is more collective and more like a singular than rafraf. Do you not see that it is collective like ʿushb (herbage), ḥaṣā (pebbles) and tamr (dates)? And you say: هذا حَصىً أبيض (these are white pebbles) and حَصىً أسود (black pebbles), because its collective use is more frequent in speech than the use of its single unit. Similar is al-ḥinṭa al-samrāʾ (brown wheat): it is singular in form and collective [in meaning]. Had it been said حنظة سُمر [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for حنطة] it would have been correct; and had it been said الشجر الخُضْر it would have been correct, as one says الحنطنة السمراء [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for الحنطة]. Another said:
* بهرجاب ما دام الأراك به خُضْراً *
(At Harjāb, as long as the arāk trees there are green.)
He said خُضْراً and did not say أخضر. All are correct. Shajar is treated as feminine and masculine. Allah said ﴿لآكِلوُنَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا البُطُون﴾, making it feminine; and He said ﴿وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾, making it masculine, and did not say فيهَا; and He said ﴿فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْه تُوقِدُونَ﴾, making it masculine.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (يس) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Letters with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «والقرآن»: [the wāw is] a particle of oath, and the thing sworn by is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) (أقسم, "I swear").

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «إنك لمن المرسلين» is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (على صراط مستقيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {الْمُرْسَلِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «تنزيل»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, i.e.: it was sent down.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «لتنذر»: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar {تَنْزِيلَ}. The clause «ما أنذر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قومًا», and the clause «فهم غافلون» is conjoined to the clause «ما أُنذر».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The preposition «على أكثرهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «حقَّ». The clause «فهم لا يؤمنون» is conjoined to the clause «حق». The clause of the implied oath is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «في أعناقهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied second object. The clause «فهي إلى الأذقان» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا», and the clause «فهم مقمحون» is conjoined to the clause «هي إلى الأذقان».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition «من بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied second object. The wāw in «ومِنْ خلفهم سدًا» conjoined the first object to the first and the second to the second. The clause «فهم لا يبصرون» is conjoined to the clause «أغشيناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «سواء»: khabar (predicate) placed first; the preposition «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «سواء». The hamza is that of equalisation (taswiya), and it together with what follows it has the force of a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the implied form is: your warning and its absence are equal. The clause of the mubtadaʾ and khabar is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا}, and the clause «لا يؤمنون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «إنما»: the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إنّ] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). The preposition «بالغيب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خشي». The clause «فبَشِّرْهُ» is conjoined to the clause «خشي».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «نحن»: tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «إن». His words «وآثارهم»: conjoined to «ما». «كلَّ»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the implied clause «أحصينا» is conjoined to the clause «نكتب», and the clause «أحصيناه» is explicative.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «واضرب» is resumptive. «أصحاب»: badal (substitute). «إذ»: a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «أصحاب», and the clause «جاءها» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «إذ»: a badal (substitute) of the first, a whole-for-whole substitute, and the fāʾs are conjunctions.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «مثلنا»: naʿt (adjective) of «بشر»; it did not become definite through the iḍāfa because it is vague. The clause «وما أنزل» is conjoined to the clause «ما أنتم إلا بشر», and «شيء» is the object of «أنزل». «إن» is negating. The clause «تكذبون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنتم», and the clause «إن أنتم إلا تكذبون» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition «إليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مرسلون», and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). The clause «إنا إليكم لمرسلون» takes the place of the two objects of «يعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The preposition «علينا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «البلاغ», and «إلا» is for restriction. The clause is conjoined to the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «لئن لم تنتهوا» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. The clause «لنرجمنكم» is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath. The clause «ليمسَّنَّكم» is conjoined to the clause that is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «أئن ذكرتم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: you took an evil omen. The clause «أنتم قوم مسرفون» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وجاء رجل» is resumptive. The clause «يسعى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل». The clause «قال» is resumptive. «يا قوم»: the one addressed, in a construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the speaker.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The second clause «اتبعوا» is a badal (substitute) of the first. The clause «وهم مهتدون» is conjoined to the clause «لا يسألكم».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «وما لي لا أعبد» is conjoined to the clause {اتَّبِعُوا}. «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the clause «لا أعبد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «ترجعون» is conjoined to the clause «فطرني», and the preposition «إليه» is attached to «ترجعون».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آلهة». «إن» is conditional. «لا تغن»: an imperfect verb, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by dropping the weak letter. «شيئا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: [availing] little or much. «ينقذون»: an imperfect verb, jussive by conjunction to the apodosis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the [remaining] nūn is that of protection (al-wiqāya), the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the implied yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: (إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «إذًا» is a particle of answer.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فاسمعون» is conjoined to the clause «آمنت».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: (قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a pronoun referring to the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb. «يا» is for drawing attention (tanbīh).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive, i.e.: they know of [my] forgiveness. The preposition «من المكرمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The wāw is resumptive. The preposition «من بعده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا». «جند»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «من السماء» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جند». The clause «وما كنا» is conjoined to the clause «ما أنزلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «إن» is negating, and the noun of «كانت» is a concealed [pronoun] referring to the punishment understood from the context. The clause «فإذا هم خامدون» is conjoined to the clause «إن كانت».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «حسرة»: the one addressed, resembling a muḍāf (shabīh bi-l-muḍāf). The preposition «على العباد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حسرة». The clause «ما يأتيهم» is resumptive; «رسول» is the fāʿil (agent), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «يأتيهم». The preposition «به» is attached to «يستهزئون».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «كم» is predicative (khabariyya), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. The preposition «من القرون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم». The clause «أهلكنا» is the object of «يروا», which is suspended [from operating] by the predicative «كم». The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنهم لا يرجعون» is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being: We decreed. The preposition «إليهم» is attached to «لا يرجعون».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The wāw is a conjunction, «إن» is negating, «كل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «لما» is a particle of restriction meaning «إلا», and «جميع» is the khabar (predicate) of «كل». «لدينا»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «محضرون»; «محضرون» is a second khabar. The clause is conjoined to the clause {أَهْلَكْنَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The wāw is resumptive. «آية»: khabar (predicate) placed first; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية»; «الأرض» is the mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «أحييناها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرض», and the clause «يأكلون» is conjoined to the clause «أخرجنا».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object. The preposition «من نخيل» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات». The two preposition and its genitive nouns «فيها من العيون» are attached to «فجَّرنا».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فجرنا». The relative «ما» is conjoined to «ثمره». The clause «يشكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «الذي»: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «آية»: khabar (predicate) placed first; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية»; «الليل» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later. The clause is conjoined to the clause «آية لهم الأرض» in verse (33). The clause «نسلخ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الليل», and the clause «فإذا هم مظلمون» is conjoined to the clause «نسلخ»; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The preposition «لها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مستقر». «والشمس» is conjoined to {اللَّيْلُ}. The clause «تجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشمس», and the clause «ذلك تقدير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The wāw is a conjunction. «القمر»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the implied clause «خلقنا» is conjoined to the clause «والليل آية لهم». «منازل»: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ in «قدَّرناه» is by removal of the preposition, i.e.: We determined for it stations; the clause «قدَّرناه» is explicative. The preposition «كالعرجون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «عاد». The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن عاد) is genitive by «حتى», attached to «قدرناه».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تدرك» is the fāʿil (agent) of «ينبغي». «سابق» is the khabar (predicate) of «الليل». The clause «وكل في فلك يسبحون» is conjoined to the clause «ولا الليل سابق», and the preposition «في فلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسبحون».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The wāw is a conjunction. «آية»: khabar (predicate) placed first, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أنَّ» and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; the implied form is: Our carrying their offspring is a sign. The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية». The clause is conjoined to the clause «آية لهم الليل» in verse (37). The preposition «في الفلك» is attached to «حملنا».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The preposition «من مثله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause {وَخَلَقْنَا}. The clause «فلا صريخ» is conjoined to the clause «نغرقهم», and the clause «ولا هم ينقذون» is conjoined to the clause «لا صريخ لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «رحمة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). The preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة», and the preposition «إلى حين» is attached to a naʿt of «متاعاً».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what follows it, i.e.: they turned away. The adverb «بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The clause «لعلكم ترحمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «وما تأتيهم» is conjoined to the conditional clause.
