The origin in the three readings is يَخْتَصِمون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Hishām transferred its fatḥa fully to the sākin before it; Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn snatched (ikhtalasā) its vowel, as a reminder that the khāʾ is originally sākin; and the rest dropped its vowel, so two sukūns met, and they gave the first of them kasra. These are four readings, read in the well-known tradition.
It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn: sukūn on the khāʾ and doubled ṣād. The grammarians find this problematic because of joining two sukūns not within their limits. A group read «يِخِصِّمُون» with kasra on the yāʾ and the khāʾ and doubled ṣād, giving the yāʾ kasra by assimilation (ittibāʿ). Ubayy read «يَخْتَصِمُون» on the original. The Shaykh said: "It is reported from the two of them, i.e. Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn, with sukūn on the khāʾ and lightened ṣād, from خَصِم." I say: this is the reading of Ḥamza, and he did not relate it from him [Translator's note: the antecedent of "he" is unclear in the source; presumably Abū Ḥayyān did not relate it from Ḥamza]. This resembles his saying {يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ} in [Sūrat] al-Baqara [v. 20], and {لاَّ يهدي} in [Sūrat] Yūnus [v. 35].

semin-durr:50-50.t: Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يُرْجَعُون» in the passive.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
And al-Aʿraj read «في الصُّوَر» with fatḥa on the wāw.
It was also read «من الأَجْدافِ», which is a dialect of «الأَجْداث» ("graves"). One says جَدَث and جَدَف, like ثُمَّ and فُمَّ, and ثُوم and فُوم. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr in one report read «يَنْسُلون» with ḍamma on the sīn. One says نَسَل الثعلبُ يَنْسِل وينسُل, i.e. "the fox hastened in its running".

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {ياويلنا}: the majority read it with annexation to the pronoun of the speakers, without feminine marker. It is «وَيْل» annexed to what follows it. Abū l-Baqāʾ related from the Kufans that «وَيْ» is a word by itself and «لنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun. End. There is no meaning for this except by a remote interpretation, which is that it be "O wonder for us", because «وي» is explained as meaning "marvel at us". Ibn Abī Laylā read «يا وَيْلتنا» with the feminine tāʾ, and from him also «يا ويْلتا» with the yāʾ replaced by alif. The interpretation of the latter is that each one of them says: «يا ويلتي».
The majority read «مَنْ» with fatḥa on the mīm, and «بَعَثَنا» as a past verb, the khabar of the interrogative «مَنْ» before it. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Nahīk read it with kasra on the mīm, as a preposition, and «بَعْثِنا» a maṣdar governed in the genitive by «مِنْ». So the first «مِنْ» is attached to «الويل» and the second to «البعث».
And «المَرْقَد» may be a maṣdar, i.e. "from our sleep", and it may be a place, being a singular put in place of a plural. The first is better, since the maṣdar is singular in all cases.
His saying: {هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ}: there are two aspects for «هذا». The more evident: that it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows is its khabar, and the pause is complete at His saying «مِنْ مَرْقَدِنا». This clause then has two aspects: one, that it is resumptive, either from the words of Allah the Exalted or from the words of the angels; two, that it is from the speech of the disbelievers, so it is in the position of the accusative by «القول». The second of the first two aspects: «هذا» is an adjective of «مَرْقَدِنا», and «ما وَعَد» is cut off from what precedes it.
Then in «ما» there are two aspects. One: that it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the khabar being implied, i.e. "that which the Most Merciful promised, and in which the messengers spoke truly, is true upon you". Al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī held this. Two: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is the promise of the Most Merciful". It was given to you at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Kahf that Ḥafṣ pauses at «مَرْقَدنا» with a slight pause, without cutting the breath, lest it be imagined that the demonstrative is a follower of «مَرْقَدِنا». These two aspects reinforce the meaning for whose sake he deliberately paused. «ما» may be a relative noun or a particle (maṣdar-forming), as its establishment was given. The two objects of "promising" and "being truthful" are omitted, i.e. "the Most Merciful promised it to us and the messengers were truthful to us"; the original is: صَدَقَنا فيه. The preposition may be removed, and you were given its like, "صَدَقني سِنَّ بَكْرِهِ", i.e. in its age. The two readings of «صيحة واحدة», accusative and nominative, were also given.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {فاليوم}: accusative by «لا تُظْلَمُ». And «شيئاً» is either a second object or a maṣdar.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {فِي شُغُلٍ}: it may be the khabar of «إنَّ», with «فاكهون» a second khabar; or «فاكهون» may be the khabar, with «في شُغُلٍ» attached to it; or it may be a ḥāl. The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with two ḍammas; the rest with ḍamma and sukūn; and they are two dialects of the Ḥijāzīs, said al-Farrāʾ. Mujāhid and Abū l-Sammāl read it with two fatḥas, and Yazīd al-Naḥwī and Ibn Hubayra with fatḥa and sukūn, and these are also two dialects.
The majority read «فاكِهون» nominative, as previously stated. Al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read «فاكهين» accusative as ḥāl, the preposition and genitive noun being the khabar. The majority also read «فاكهين» with alif, meaning "possessors of fruit", like لابنٍ and تامرٍ and لاحمٍ; while al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rajāʾ, Shayba, Qatāda and Mujāhid read «فَكِهون» without alif, meaning "delighted, rejoicing", from al-fukāha with ḍamma. It was said: al-fākih and al-fakih have the sense of one who takes pleasure and enjoys comfort, because both fruit (fākiha) and jest (fukāha) are among what is enjoyed and delighted in. «فَكِهيْن» was read with the short form and yāʾ, as stated, and «فَكُهُوْن» with the short form and ḍamma on the kāf. One says: رجلٌ فَكِهٌ وفَكُهٌ, like رَجُلٍ نَدِس ونَدُسٍ, and حَذِر وحَذُر.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ}: «هم» may be an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent pronoun in «فاكهون», with «أزواجُهم» conjoined to the latent pronoun. It may also be an emphasis of the latent pronoun in «شُغُل» if we make it the khabar, with «أزواجُهم» likewise conjoined to it. The Shaykh stated it so. There is something to consider in it, in that the emphasized and the emphasis are separated by the khabar of «إنَّ». Its parallel is that you say: "إن زيداً في الدار قائمٌ هو وعمروٌ", making «هو» an emphasis of the pronoun in your «في الدار». On these two aspects His saying «متكِئون» is another khabar of «إنَّ», and «في [ظلال]» is attached to it or is a ḥāl, and «على الأرائِك» is attached to it. «هم» may also be a mubtadaʾ with «متكئون» its khabar, the two prepositional phrases as before. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «في ظلالٍ» to be the khabar. He said: "«وعلى الأرائِكِ» is resumptive"; this is an expression that gives a mistaken impression, and he means by it that «متكئون» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source continues with an apparently garbled clause, «و «متكئون» مبتدأٌ مؤخرٌ إذ لا معنى له», "and «متكئون» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, since it has no meaning"; translated as it stands]. ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read «متكئين» accusative as ḥāl.
The two brothers read «في ظُلَلٍ» with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ and short, which is the plural of ظُلَّة, like غُرْفَة and غُرَف, and حُلَّة and حُلَل; it is an expression for carpets and curtains. The rest read it with kasra on the ẓāʾ and an alif, again a plural of ظُلَّة, like حُلَّة and حِلال, and بُرْمة and بِرام; or a plural of فِعْلة with kasra, since one says ظُلَّة and ظِلَّة with ḍamma and kasra, so it is like لِقْحة and لِقاح, except that فِعال is not analogical for it; or a plural of فِعْل, like ذِئْب and ذِئاب, and ريْح and رِياح.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {مَّا يَدَّعُونَ}: there are three aspects in this «ما»: a relative noun; an indefinite noun that is qualified (and the returning pronoun in these two is omitted); and maṣdar-forming. And يَدَّعُون is the imperfect of ادَّعَى, the pattern iftaʿala, from دعا يَدْعو, and it has taken in the meaning of wishing. Abū ʿUbayda said: "The Arabs say: ادَّعِ عَلَيَّ ما شِئْتَ, i.e. wish (for what you want)", and "so-and-so is in the best of what he يَدَّعي", i.e. what he wishes. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is from invocation (duʿāʾ), i.e. what they call for, the people of Paradise are given, from دَعَوْتُ غلامي ('I called my servant')." And it was said: iftaʿala in the sense of tafāʿala, i.e. what they call to one another for, like their saying ارتَمَوْا and ترامَوْا in the same sense. «ما» is a mubtadaʾ. Its khabar has two aspects: one, the apparent one, that it is the preposition and genitive noun before it; the second, that it is «سلامٌ», i.e. "pure, safe" or "possessing safety".

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {سَلاَمٌ}: the majority read it nominative. Several aspects: one, as stated before, that it is the khabar of «ما يَدَّعون». Two: that it is a badal from it; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The Shaykh said: "If it were a badal, «ما يَدَّعُون» would be specific, whereas the apparent sense is that it is general, for all that they call for; and if it is general, it is not a badal from it." Three: that it is an adjective of «ما», and this is when you make it an indefinite that is qualified; but if you make it a relative («الذي») or maṣdar-forming, that is impossible because of their differing in definiteness and indefiniteness. Four: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is peace". Five: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the verb that governs «قَوْلاً» in the accusative, i.e. "peace, said to them as a saying"; and it was said that its estimation is: "Peace upon you." Six: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «مِنْ رَبٍ», with «قولاً» a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, which with its governor is parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.
Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh and ʿĪsā read «سَلاماً» accusative. It has two aspects. One: that it is a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. 'they have what they desire, pure'." The second: that it is the maṣdar of "they greet with a greeting", either from salutation or from safety. And «قَوْلاً» is either a confirming maṣdar or accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is the most apt." And «مِنْ رَبٍّ» is either an adjective of «قَوْلاً» or the khabar of «سَلامٌ», as stated. Al-Qaraẓī read «سِلْمٌ» with kasra and sukūn. The difference between the two was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {وامتازوا}: on an implied saying that corresponds to what was said to the believers, i.e. "and it is said to the criminals: separate yourselves", i.e. withdraw, from مازه يَمِيزه.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {أَعْهَدْ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza, on the original for the imperfect prefix. Ṭalḥa and al-Hudhayl ibn Sharaḥbīl al-Kūfī read it with kasra. It has already been stated that this is a dialect for the imperfect prefix, under conditions mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Fātiḥa, and there was an anecdote there. Ibn Wathāb read «أَحَّدْ» with a doubled ḥāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm, and from it is «دَحَّا مَحَّا», i.e. 'leave it with it'; the hāʾ was turned into ḥāʾ, then the ʿayn into ḥāʾ, when assimilation was intended. The better is to say that the ʿayn was replaced by ḥāʾ, which is the dialect of Hudhayl; and when it was assimilated the second was turned into the first, which is the reverse of the chapter of assimilation. Its verification was given at the end of [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān." Ibn Khālawayh said: "Ibn Wathāb and al-Hudhayl read «أَلَمْ إعْهَدْ» with kasra on the mīm and the hamza and fatḥa on the hāʾ, which is according to the dialect of one who gives kasra to the first of the imperfect other than the yāʾ. It is reported from Ibn Wathāb «اعْهِد» with kasra on the hāʾ. One says عَهِد and عَهَد." End. By "kasra on the mīm and the hamza" he means that the origin of this reading is that the imperfect prefix was given kasra, then its vowel was transferred to the mīm and it was given kasra; not that the kasra is present in wording in the mīm and the hamza, since that would require the hamza being a cutting hamza and vowelling the mīm without cause. As for the kasra of the hāʾ, it is because it was heard that in the past tense «عَهَدَ» has fatḥa. His saying "other than the yāʾ", and so said al-Zamakhsharī, is the well-known; and it has been reported from some of Kalb that they give the yāʾ kasra, saying يِعْلَمُ.
Al-Zamakhsharī said of it: "Al-Zajjāj allowed it to be of the type نَعِمَ يَنْعِمُ and ضَرَب يَضْرِب." He means that its explanation is one of two aspects: either an irregularity in what combines فَعِل يَفْعِلُ with kasra in both, like نَعِمَ يَنْعِمُ, حَسِب يَحْسِبُ and بَئِسَ يَبْئِسُ, words that I counted in [Sūrat] al-Baqara; or that fatḥa was heard in its past, like ضَرَبَ, as Ibn Khālawayh related. Al-Zamakhsharī related that «أَحْهَدْ» was read, with the ʿayn replaced by ḥāʾ, and it was already stated that it is the dialect of Hudhayl; and this strengthens that the origin of «أَحَّد» is أَحْهَد, assimilated as stated.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {جِبِلاًّ}: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read it with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ and doubled lām. Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir with ḍamma and sukūn. The rest with two ḍammas, the lām lightened in both. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Zuhrī and Ibn Hurmuz with two ḍammas and doubled lām. Al-Aʿmash with two kasras and lightened lām. Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, al-Yamānī and Ḥammād ibn Salama with kasra and sukūn. These are dialects of this word. Its meaning was given at the end of [Sūrat] al-Shuʿarāʾ. «جِبَلاً» was also read with kasra on the jīm and fatḥa on the bāʾ, plural of جِبْلَة like فِطَر plural of فِطْرَة. The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī read «جِيْلاً» with yāʾ (two dots below), which is clear.
The majority read: «أفلَمْ تكونوا» addressing the children of Ādam. Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read it with the yāʾ of third person, the pronoun being for the jibill. It would be fitting for them both to read {التي كانوا يُوعَدُونَ}, were it not that they excuse it by iltifāt.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {اليوم نَخْتِمُ}: «اليومَ» is an adverb for what follows. «يُخْتَمُ» was read in the passive, the prepositional phrase after it standing in place of its agent.
«تَتَكلَّمُ» was read with two tāʾs (above). «ولْتَتَكَلَّمْ ولْتَشْهَدْ» was read with the lām of command. Ṭalḥa read «ولِتُكَلِّمَنا ولِتَشهدَ» with the lām of purpose (lām kay) putting the verb in the subjunctive, its attachment being omitted, i.e. "We sealed for the sake of speaking and testifying". And «بما كانوا» means: "of that which they used to do", or "because of their being earners".

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {فاستبقوا}: conjoined to «لَطَمَسْنا», and this is by way of supposition and estimation. ʿĪsā read «فاسْتَبِقوا» as an imperative, on an implied saying, i.e. "so it is said to them: race". And «الصِّراطَ» is, according to the majority, a specific adverb of place; therefore they interpreted the verb's reaching it either as its being a direct object in a figurative sense, making it the thing raced against rather than that raced to, with «اسْتَبَقُوا» containing the sense of "hastened"; or on omission of the preposition, i.e. "to the path". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is accusative as an adverb, and that goes along with the view of Ibn al-Ṭarāwa, for «الصراط», «الطريق» and the like are not specific according to him. But Sībawayh [holds] that his saying:
3787 - لَدْنٌ بِهَزِّ الكَفِّ يَعْسِلُ مَتْنُهُ ... فيه كما عَسَلَ الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(Supple when the hand shakes it, its shaft quivers as the fox runs along the road.)
is a necessity, because of putting «الطريق» in the accusative." [Translator's note: the source reads «إلاَّ أنَّ سيبويهِ: على أن قوله», which seems slightly garbled; rendered as it stands.]

semin-durr:67-67.t:
Abū Bakr read «مَكاناتِهم» in the plural, and it was given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām. The majority read «مُضِيَّاً» with ḍamma on the mīm, a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿūl; its origin is مُضُوْي, assimilated, and what precedes the yāʾ was given kasra so that it would be sound, like لُقِيّا.
Abū Ḥaywa read it, and it was reported from al-Kisāʾī, with kasra on the mīm by assimilation to the vowel of the ʿayn, like «عِتِيًّا» and «صِلِيَّاً». It was also read with fatḥa. It is one of the maṣdars that came on faʿīl, like al-rasīm and al-dhamīl.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {نُنَكِّسْهُ}: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with ḍamma on the first nūn, fatḥa on the second and kasra on the doubled kāf, from نَكَّسَه, for intensification. The rest read it with fatḥa on the first, sukūn on the second and ḍamma on the lightened kāf, from نَكَسَه, which admits intensification or not. It was already given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām that Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read «تَعْقِلون» in the second person, and the rest in the third.

semin-durr:69-69.t: His saying: {إِنْ هُوَ}: i.e. "it is only the Qur'an", indicated by the context; or "knowledge is only a reminder", indicated by «وما عَلَّمْناه». The pronoun in «له» is for the Prophet ﷺ. And it was said: for the Qur'an.

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying: {لِّيُنذِرَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read here, and in [Sūrat] al-Aḥqāf, «لتنذرَ» in the second person. The rest in the third, with a divergence from al-Bazzī in al-Aḥqāf. The third person admits that the pronoun in it be for the Prophet ﷺ, and that it be for the Qur'an. Al-Jaḥdarī and al-Yamānī read «لِيُنْذِرَ» in the passive. Abū l-Sammāl and al-Yamānī also read «لِيَنْذَرَ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the dhāl, from نَذِر with kasra on the dāl, i.e. "knew", so «مَنْ» is the agent.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {رَكُوبُهُمْ}: i.e. their mount (مَرْكوبهم), like al-ḥalūb and al-ḥaṣūr in the sense of the passive, which is not analogical. Ubayy and ʿĀʾisha read «رَكوبَتُهم» with the tāʾ. Some counted the entry of the tāʾ on this pattern as irregular, and al-Zamakhsharī, in the view of some, made the two (رَكوب and رَكوبة) a plural, meaning a collective noun (ism jamʿ), otherwise this pattern has not occurred among the plural forms. Ibn Mālik also counted the patterns of collective nouns and did not mention faʿūla among them. Al-Ḥasan, Abū l-Burhasm and al-Aʿmash read «رُكوبُهم» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and an annexed noun must be omitted, either from the first, i.e. "so of its benefits is their riding", or from the second, i.e. "possessing their riding". Ibn Khālawayh said: "The Arabs say: ناقَةٌ رَكُوْبٌ ورَكُوْبَةٌ, حَلُوب وحَلُوْبَة, رَكْباةٌ حَلْباةٌ, رَكَبُوْتٌ حَلَبُوْت, رَكَبى حَلَبى, رَكَبُوْتا حَلَبُوْتا [ورَكْبانَةٌ حَلْبانَة]," and he recited: 3788 - رَكْبانَةٍ حَلْبَانَةٍ زَفُوْفِ ... تَخْلِطُ بينَ وَبَرٍ موصُوْفِ
(A she-camel for riding and for milking, swift, mixing between hair that is described.)
And al-mashārib is the plural of mashrab with fatḥa, as a maṣdar or a place. The pronoun in «لا يَسْتَطيعون» is either for the gods or for their worshippers; likewise the pronouns after it. The reading «يَحْزُن» and «يُحزن» was given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ونسي خالقَه» on the pattern of the active participle.

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ}: it was said: in the sense of fāʿil. And it was said: in the sense of mafʿūl; on the first, the absence of the tāʾ is not analogical. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-ramīm is a noun for what has decayed of bones, not an adjective, like al-rimma and al-rufāt; so it cannot be asked 'why was it not made feminine when it occurred as the khabar of a feminine?', nor is it faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil or mafʿūl."

semin-durr:80-80.t: His saying: {الأخضر}: this is the reading of the majority. «الخضراء» was also read, regarding the meaning. It has already been stated that the generic noun may be masculine or feminine. The Exalted said: {نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20] and {نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7]. It was also given that the Banū Tamīm and Najd make it masculine, and the Ḥijāz make it feminine, except for words that are excepted.

semin-durr:81-81.t: His saying: {بِقَادِرٍ}: this is the reading of the majority; the bāʾ entered redundantly on the active participle. Al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿraj read «يَقْدِرُ» as an imperfect verb. The pronoun in «مِثْلهم» was said to return to the people, because they are the ones addressed; and it was said: to the heavens and the earth, because they include those who have intellect. And «بَلَى» is an answer to «ليس», even if the interrogative that turns it into an affirmative enters it. The majority read «الخَلاَّق», an intensive form; al-Jaḥdarī, al-Ḥasan and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «الخالق» as an active participle. The disagreement over «فيكون», accusative and nominative, and its explanation, were given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:83-83.t: Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash read «مَلَكَة» on the pattern of شجرَة. «مَمْلَكَةُ» was read on the pattern of mafʿala, and «ملك» was also read. And «المَلَكُوْتُ» is the most intensive of all. The majority read «تُرْجَعون» in the passive, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī in the active.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يس (١) وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ (٢)).
The majority read the nūn with a sukūn, and its counterpart has been mentioned [Translator's note: i.e. earlier in the book]. Some of them pronounce the nūn distinctly (iẓhār), because by that he makes its sukūn real, whereas in the nasalisation (ghunna) there is something that brings it close to a vowel for the sake of pure continuous reading; and in the iẓhār there is a bringing of the letter close to pausing on it.
Some of them give the nūn a kasra, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two sukūns, and some of them give it a fatḥa, just as the fatḥa is given in أَيْنَ; and it has been said: the fatḥa is a case-ending (iʿrāb). And (يس) is a name of the sura, like هَابِيل [Translator's note: i.e. a non-Arabic proper name, and so a diptote], and the implied form is: "Recite Yā Sīn" (اتْلُ يس). (وَالْقِرَانِ) [Translator's note: so spelled in the source]: an oath on every view.

ukberi-tibyan:3-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (٣) عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٤) تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ (٥) لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أُنْذِرَ آبَاؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى صِرَاطٍ): it is a second khabar (predicate) of إنّ [Translator's note: the source prints لَإِنْ], and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase.
(تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ), i.e. "it is the sending down of the Mighty" (هُوَ تَنْزِيلُ الْعَزِيزِ); the maṣdar (verbal noun) has the meaning of the passive participle, i.e. "that which is sent down by the Mighty" (مُنَزَّلُ الْعَزِيزِ). It is read in the accusative, as a maṣdar, i.e. "with a sending down" (تَنْزِيلًا); and also in the genitive, as an adjective of «الْقُرْآن».
(لِتُنْذِرَ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَنْزِيل, or attached to the meaning of His saying «مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ», i.e. "sent so that you may warn" (مُرْسَلٌ لِتُنْذِرَ).
And (مَا) is negating. It has been said: it has the meaning of الَّذِي (the relative "which"), i.e. "you warn them of the punishment of which their forefathers were warned" (تُنْذِرُهُمُ الْعَذَابَ الَّذِي أَنْذَرَهُ آبَاؤُهُمْ).
It has been said: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa). And it has been said: it is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ): with ghayn, i.e. "We covered the eyes of their insight"; so the muḍāf (first term of the construct) is omitted.
It is also read with ʿayn [Translator's note: i.e. فَأَعْشَيْنَاهُمْ], i.e. "We weakened their insight from perceiving guidance", just as the eye of one with night-blindness (الْأَعْشَى) is weak.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا وَآثَارَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ): like (وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ) [al-Isrāʾ: 13], and it has already been dealt with.

ukberi-tibyan:13-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ (١٣) إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ): «اضْرِبْ» here has the meaning of "make" (اجْعَلْ); «أَصْحَابَ» is the first mafʿūl (object), and «مَثَلًا» is the second mafʿūl.
It has been said: it has the meaning of "mention" (اذْكُرْ), and the implied form is: "a likeness, the likeness of the people" (مَثَلًا مِثْلَ أَصْحَابِ); so the second is a badal (substitute) from the first.
And (إِذْ جَاءَهَا) is like «إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ», and it has already been dealt with.
And the second (إِذْ) is a badal (substitute) from the first.
(فَعَزَزْنَا) is read with a doubled consonant and with a single one, and the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, i.e. "We strengthened the two of them" (قَوَّيْنَاهُمَا).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ): in the form of a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "if you are reminded, you disbelieve" (إِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ كَفَرْتُمْ), or the like.
It is also read with a fatḥa on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. أَأَنْ], i.e. "because you were reminded" (لِأَنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ). And it is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: «أَيْنَ ذُكِرْتُمْ», i.e. "your evil deed clings to you wherever you are mentioned"; and the kāf is without doubling on this view.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا لِيَ): the majority read the yāʾ with a fatḥa, because what follows it is treated as joined to it, since it is not good to pause on it and begin with what follows it. And (مَالِي لَا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ) is the reverse of that.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَأَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي): it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and «مَا» may not stand in place of «لَا» here, because «مَا» negates what is in the present, whereas the apodosis of a condition is future and nothing else.

ukberi-tibyan:26-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ (٢٦) بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي): there are three views on «مَا». The first: it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), i.e. "of His forgiving" (بِغُفْرَانِهِ). The second: it has the meaning of الَّذِي, i.e. "of the sin which He forgave" (بِالذَّنْبِ الَّذِي غَفَرَهُ). The third: it is an interrogative expressing magnification; some people mentioned it, and it is far-fetched, because when a preposition comes before the interrogative «مَا», its alif is dropped; though it has occurred in poetry without the dropping.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا): «مَا» is negating, and likewise in «وَمَا كُنَّا».
It is also permissible that the second «مَا» be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "and indeed We were" (وَقَدْ كُنَّا).
And it has been said: it is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «جُنْدٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً): the noun (ism) of كَانَ is implied (muḍmar), i.e. "the cry was nothing but a cry" (مَا كَانَتِ الصَّيْحَةُ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً); the purpose is to describe it as single. And إِذَا is for surprise (mufājaʾa). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:30-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٣٠) أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَاحَسْرَةً): there are two views on it. The first: «حَسْرَةً» is the one addressed (munādā), i.e. "O regret, come! For this is your time."
And (عَلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَسْرَة; that is why it was put in the accusative, as in your saying: "O you who are striking a man" (يَا ضَارِبًا رَجُلًا). The second: the one addressed is omitted, and «حَسْرَةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I lament with a lament" (أَتَحَسَّرُ حَسْرَةً).
It is read among the irregular (shādhdh) readings «يَا حَسْرَةَ الْعِبَادِ», i.e. "O their lamenting!" (يَا تَحْسِيرَهُمْ); so the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. It may also be annexed to its object, i.e. "I lament over the servants" (أَتَحَسَّرُ عَلَى الْعِبَادِ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ): the clause is an explanation of the cause of the regret.
(وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا): it has already been dealt with.
(وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ): with a fatḥa on the hamza; it is maṣdariyya, and the position of the clause is a badal (substitute) from the position of «كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا»; the implied form is: "Have they not seen that they [will not return] to them" (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ).
It is also read with a kasra on the hamza, as a resumptive (istiʾnāf) clause.

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ): it has been dealt with at the end of Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ): [«آيَةٌ»] is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَهُمْ» the khabar (predicate). And «الْأَرْضُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَحْيَيْنَاهَا» its khabar; the clause is an explanation of the sign.
It has been said: «الْأَرْضُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «آيَةٌ» is a fronted khabar, «أَحْيَيْنَاهَا» is the explanation of the sign, and «لَهُمْ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «آيَةٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ (٣٤) لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْعُيُونِ): مِنْ, according to the view of al-Akhfash, is redundant (zāʾida); according to the view of others, the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, i.e. "[We caused to gush forth] from the springs what they benefit from" (مِنَ الْعُيُونِ مَا يَنْتَفِعُونَ بِهِ).
(وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ): there are three views on «مَا». The first: it has the meaning of الَّذِي. The second: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa). On both these views it is in the position of a genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ثَمَرَةٍ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «ثَمَرِهِ»]; and it may be accusative, [conjoined] to the position of (مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ).
The third: it is negating.
It is also read without the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. وَمَا عَمِلَتْ]; the three views are possible, except that [taking it as] negating is weak, because «عَمِلَتْ» has no object mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:39-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّى عَادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ (٣٩) لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَهَا أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْقَمَرُ): in the nominative, it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قَدَّرْنَاهُ» is the khabar (predicate).
And in the accusative, by an implied verb, i.e. "and We measured out the moon" (وَقَدَّرْنَا الْقَمَرَ), because it is conjoined to a noun on which a verb has operated, so it was construed accordingly.
Whoever reads the nominative says: it is construed on (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ) in the two places, and on (الشَّمْسُ), and these are nouns on which no verb has operated.
And (مَنَازِلَ), i.e. "possessing stations" (ذَا مَنَازِلَ); so it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second mafʿūl (object), because قَدَّرْنَا has the meaning of "We made [it] become" (صَيَّرْنَا). It has been said: the implied form is: "We measured out stations for it" (قَدَّرْنَا لَهُ مَنَازِلَ).
And (الْعُرْجُونُ) is on the pattern فُعْلُول, and the nūn is a root letter.
It has been said: it is augmentative, because it is from الِانْعِرَاج (bending); this is sound in meaning, but irregular in usage.
Some read (سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ) with the accusative [Translator's note: i.e. سَابِقُ النَّهَارَ]; this is weak, and its permissibility rests on the tanwīn having been dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.
And «يُسَبِّحُونَ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «يَسْبَحُونَ»] is construed as referring to rational beings because they are described with running, swimming, overtaking and outstripping.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّا): it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that We…" (هِيَ أَنَّا).
It has been said: it is a mubtadaʾ, and «آيَةٌ لَهُمْ» is the khabar; this is permissible because «أَنَّا» is connected with what precedes it.
The hāʾ and the mīm in (ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ) refer to the people of Nūḥ; and it has been said: to the people of Mecca.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ (٤٣)).
(فَلَا صَرِيخَ): the majority read it with a fatḥa, and what follows it is then resumptive.
It has been read with the nominative and tanwīn; its explanation is what we mentioned at His saying: (فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَمَتَاعًا إِلَى حِينٍ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun).
It has been said: the implied form is "except by a mercy" (إِلَّا بِرَحْمَةٍ). And it has been said: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ (٤٩)).
(يَخِصِّمُونَ): like His saying (يَهْدِي) [Translator's note: i.e. يَهِدِّي in Yūnus 35], and it has been dealt with in Yūnus.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا مَنْ بَعَثَنَا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنَا هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَصَدَقَ الْمُرْسَلُونَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَاوَيْلَنَا): it is like His saying: (يَاحَسْرَةً).
The Kufans said: «وَيْ» is a word, and «لَنَا» is a preposition and its genitive noun.
The majority take «مَنْ بَعَثَنَا» as an interrogative. It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: مِنْ بَعْثِنَا [Translator's note: the source prints «مَنْ بَعَثَنَا»; the reading meant is with the preposition مِنْ and the maṣdar], taken as a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَيْل.
And (هَذَا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مَا وَعَدَ» is the khabar (predicate); «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or is maṣdariyya.
It has been said: هَذَا is a naʿt (adjective) of مَرْقَدِنَا, so one pauses on it; and «مَا وَعَدَ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is true" (حَقٌّ) or the like; or it is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "this is" (هَذَا), or "[what] raised us is" (بَعَثَنَا).

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي شُغُلٍ): it is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and «فَاكِهُونَ» is a second khabar; or it [Translator's note: i.e. «فَاكِهُونَ»] is the khabar, and «فِي شُغُلٍ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
It is also read (فَاكِهِينَ), as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase.
And الشُّغُل — with two ḍammas, with a ḍamma followed by a sukūn, with two fatḥas, and with a fatḥa followed by a sukūn — these are dialectal forms, and it has been read with all of them.

ukberi-tibyan:56-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ (٥٦) لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَلَهُمْ مَا يَدَّعُونَ (٥٧) سَلَامٌ قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي ظِلَالٍ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of «هُمْ».
And (عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ) is then resumptive. Or the khabar may be «مُتَّكِئُونَ», with «فِي ظِلَالٍ» a ḥāl (circumstantial) and «عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ» in the accusative by مُتَّكِئُونَ.
And ظِلَال is the plural of ظِلّ, like ذِئْب and ذِئَاب; or of ظُلَّة, like قُبَّة and قِبَاب. And الظُّلَل is the plural of ظُلَّة and nothing else.
(مَا يَدَّعُونَ): there are three views on «مَا»:
It has the meaning of الَّذِي; or it is an indefinite noun; or it is maṣdariyya. Its position is that of a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar is «لَهُمْ». It has been said: the khabar is «سَلَامٌ». It has been said: «سَلَامٌ» is a second adjective (ṣifa) of «مَا». It has been said: «سَلَامٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is peace" (هُوَ سَلَامٌ). And it has been said: it is a badal (substitute) from «مَا».
It is also read in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted hāʾ, i.e. "possessing safety" (ذَا سَلَامَةٍ) or "safe and sound" (مُسْلِمًا).
And (قَوْلًا) is a maṣdar, i.e. "Allah says that to them as a saying" (يَقُولُ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا), or "they say [it] as a saying" (يَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا).
And (مِنْ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of قَوْل.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْقِلُونَ (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جِبِلًّا): there are many readings of it; all of them are dialectal forms with one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:69-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ الشِّعْرَ وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ (٦٩) لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ هُوَ): the pronoun refers to what was taught, i.e. "what He taught him is nothing but a reminder"; «وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ» indicates it. (لِتُنْذِرَ): with tāʾ, as address [to the Prophet], and with yāʾ as third person [referring to him], or on the view that it refers to the Qurʾān.

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ (٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَكُوبُهُمْ): with a fatḥa on the rāʾ, i.e. "what they ride" (مَرْكُوبُهُمْ), just as they say حَلُوب with the meaning of مَحْلُوب (milked).
It has been said: it expresses relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing riding" (ذُو رَكُوبٍ).
It has been read «رَكُوبَتُهُمْ», with tāʾ, like حَلُوبَتُهُمْ. And it is read with a ḍamma on the rāʾ, i.e. "that which possesses their riding" (ذُو رَكُوبِهِمْ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; presumably ذُو رُكُوبِهِمْ is meant]; or the maṣdar (verbal noun) has the meaning of the passive participle, like الْخَلْق (creation, i.e. what is created).

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًا وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قَالَ مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ): with the meaning of رَامّ (decaying) [Translator's note: the source prints «رَامِمٍ»], or of مَرْمُوم (decayed).

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (٨٢)).
(كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): it has been dealt with in Sūrat al-Naḥl. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Yā Sīn
Meccan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis that ﴿يس﴾ means: ”يا إنْسانُ“ ("O human being"); it has also come as: ”يا رَجُلُ“ ("O man"), and as: ”يا مُحَمَّدُ“ ("O Muḥammad"). What the experts in Arabic hold is that it is in the position of ”الـم“ — an opening of the sūra. It has also come that it means an oath. Some of them — I mean some of the Arabs — say: ”ياسِينَ والقُرْآنَ“, with fatḥa on the nūn; this is permissible in Arabic, but the sukūn is better, because these are letters of the alphabet, and we have explained the like of this. As for the one who gives it fatḥa, it is on two accounts: either ”يـس“ is a name of the sūra, quoted as is (ḥikāya), as though he said: "Recite Yā Sīn", and it is on the pattern of ”هابِيلَ“ and ”قابِيلَ“, a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf); or it may be that he gave it fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿والقُرْآنِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ ("by the wise Qurʾān"): its meaning is that its verses have been made firm, and in them have been made clear the command, the prohibition, the parables and the stories of the bygone nations.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿إنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ("you are indeed among the messengers"): this is an address to Muḥammad ﷺ, and it is the answer to the oath, the answer of ”والقُرْآنِ إنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ“.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ ("on a straight path"), that is: on the way of the prophets who preceded you. The best [analysis] in Arabic is that ”لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“, and ”عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ“ a second khabar; so the meaning is: "you are indeed among the messengers who were sent upon a straight way".

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿تَنْـزِيلَ العَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ ("a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful"). It is read ”تَنْزِيلُ“ with the nominative and [with] the accusative. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "Allah has sent that down as a sending-down"; and whoever reads it in the nominative takes it in the sense: "what has been sent down to you is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful".

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا ما أُنْذِرَ آباؤُهم فَهم غافِلُونَ﴾ ("that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless"). It has come in the exegesis: "that you may warn a people with the like of what their forefathers were warned with"; and it has come: "that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned", in which case ”ما“ is a negation. This — and Allah knows best — is the preferred view, because His saying ”فَهم غافِلُونَ“ is evidence for the meaning "their forefathers were not warned"; whereas if their forefathers had been warned [and yet] "they are heedless", there is something far-fetched in it — but it has come in the exegesis. The evidence for the negation is His saying: ﴿وَما آتَيْناهم مِن كُتُبٍ يَدْرُسُونَها وما أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِن نَذِيرٍ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 44]; had their forefathers been warned, they would have been warned and studying books — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿لَقَدْ حَقَّ القَوْلُ عَلى أكْثَرِهِمْ﴾ ("the word has indeed come true against most of them"). ”اَلْقَوْلُ“ here — and Allah knows best — is like His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. The meaning is: "the word has come true against most of them because of their disbelief and obstinacy; Allah led them astray and withheld them from guidance".

zajjaj:8-8.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا في أعْناقِهِمْ أغْلالا﴾ ("We have put shackles on their necks"). Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd — may Allah have mercy on them — read: ”إنّا جَعَلْنا في أيْمانِهِمْ“ ("on their right hands"), and some read: ”في أيْدِيهِمْ أغْلالًا“ ("on their hands"). Neither of these two readings should be recited, because they differ from the muṣḥaf. The meaning in His saying ”في أعْناقِهِمْ“, and [in the reading of] whoever read ”في أيْمانِهِمْ“, and whoever read ”في أيْدِيهِمْ“, is one and the same; that is because the shackle is not on the neck without the hand, nor on the hand without the neck. So the meaning is: "We have put shackles on their necks and on their right hands". ﴿فَهِيَ إلى الأذْقانِ﴾ ("and they reach to the chins") is an allusion (kināya) to the hands, not to the necks, because the shackle makes the hand adjoin the chin; the neck is already close to the chin — the shackle does not bring the neck to the chin.
And His saying: ﴿فَهم مُقْمَحُونَ﴾ ("so their heads are forced up"): ”اَلْمُقْمَحُ“ is the one who raises his head and lowers his gaze. The two months of Kānūn are called ”شَهْرا قِماحٍ“ ("the two months of head-raising"), because when the camels come to the water they raise their heads on account of its intense cold; hence "the two months of qimāḥ" is said. The necks were mentioned and the hands were not mentioned only for brevity and concision, because the shackle includes the neck and the hand; and whoever reads ”في أيْمانِهِمْ“ — that too indicates the neck. Similar to this is the saying of al-Muthaqqib:
؎فَما أدْرِي إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضًا ∗∗∗ أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِينِي؟
(I do not know, when I head for a land seeking good, which of the two will meet me:)
أألْخَيْرُ الَّذِي أنا أبْتَغِيهِ ... أمِ الشَّرُّ الَّذِي هو يَبْتَغِينِي
(the good that I am seeking, or the evil that is seeking me?)
He mentioned the good alone and then said ”أيُّهُما يَلِينِي“ ("which of the two will meet me"), because it is already known that good and evil are both laid before a person; he does not know, when he heads for a land, whether this or that will meet him. Similar to it in the Book of Allah is: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81] ("garments that protect you from the heat"), and He did not mention the cold, because what protects from this protects from that.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا﴾ ("and We have put before them a barrier"), and ”سُدًّا“ — with fatḥa and with ḍamma — and their meaning is one. It has been said: ”اَلسَّدُّ“ is the work of a human being, and ”اَلسُّدُّ“ is the natural form of what is blocked. There are two ways in it. One of them has come in the exegesis: some people intended harm to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah came between them and that, so they were made like one in this state: they were made like one whose right hand has been shackled, whose way has been blocked before him and behind him, and over whose sight a covering has been put — and that is the meaning of ﴿فَأغْشَيْناهُمْ﴾ ("and We have covered them"); it is also read ”فَأعْشَيْناهم“, with an undotted ʿayn ("We have dimmed their sight"). So Allah came between them and His Messenger; and among these was Abū Jahl, according to what is related. And it is possible that He is describing their being led astray, so He said: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا في أعْناقِهِمْ أغْلالا فَهي إلى الأذْقانِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 8], that is: We led them astray, and held back their hands from spending in the way of Allah and from striving in what brings one near to Allah; ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا ومِن خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا﴾, just as He said: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 7] — the verse. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿وَسَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أأنْذَرْتَهم أمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 10], because whoever Allah has led astray in this way, warning does not benefit him.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿إنَّما تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ﴾ ("you only warn the one who follows the Reminder"), that is: the one who listens to the Qurʾān and follows it. ﴿وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالغَيْبِ﴾ ("and fears the Most Merciful unseen"), that is: fears Allah where no one sees him. ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وأجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ ("so give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward"). The meaning is: "whoever follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful, give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward". ”اَلْمَغْفِرَةُ“ is the pardoning of his sins, and ”أجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ“ is through Paradise.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي المَوْتى ونَكْتُبُ ما قَدَّمُوا وآثارَهُمْ﴾ ("it is We who give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and their traces"): what they have put forward of their deeds; and We record their traces, that is: whoever establishes a good practice, its reward is recorded for him, and whoever establishes an evil practice, its punishment is recorded against him. It has also been said: ”وَنَكْتُبُ آثارَهم“, that is: their footsteps. The first is more common and clearer.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
﴿واضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلا﴾ ("and strike for them a parable"). ”مَثَلًا“ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The meaning of people's saying ”اِضْرِبْ لَهُ مَثَلًا“ is: "mention to him a parable". It is said: ”عِنْدِي مِن هَذا الضَّرْبِ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ“ ("I have much of this kind"), that is: of this pattern; and you say: "these things are of one ḍarb", that is: of one pattern. So ”اِضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلًا“ means: ”مَثِّلْ لَهم مَثَلًا“ ("present to them a likeness").
And His saying: ﴿أصْحابَ القَرْيَةِ﴾ ("the people of the town"), that is: "the story of the people of the town". ﴿إذْ جاءَها المُرْسَلُونَ﴾ ("when the messengers came to it"): it has come in the exegesis that they were the people of Antioch; ʿĪsā sent two [messengers] to them, and they called them liars. He said: ﴿فَعَزَّزْنا بِثالِثٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 14] ("so We reinforced them with a third"); it is read ”فَعَزَزْنا“ with shadda and without [i.e. فَعَزَّزْنا and فَعَزَزْنا]. The meaning of ”فَعَزَّزْنا“ is: We strengthened and reinforced the message with a third, that is: with a third messenger. ﴿فَقالُوا إنّا إلَيْكم مُرْسَلُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 14], up to His saying: ﴿البَلاغُ المُبِينُ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 17]: so the messengers informed them that what was incumbent on them was [only] the conveying [of the message].

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿قالُوا إنّا تَطَيَّرْنا بِكُمْ﴾ ("they said: We augur evil from you"), that is: we take you as an ill omen. ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾ ("if you do not desist we will surely stone you"), that is: we will surely kill you by stoning.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿قالُوا طائِرُكم مَعَكُمْ﴾ ("they said: Your omen is with you"). ”طَيْرُكم مَعَكم“ is also permissible, because one says ”طائِرٌ“ and ”طَيْرٌ“ with one meaning; but I do not know anyone who read ”طَيْرُكم“ here, without the alif. The meaning is: "they said: your ill luck is with you". ﴿أإنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾ ("[is it] because you are reminded?"), that is: "If you are reminded, do you augur evil?!" It is also read: ”أأنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ“, that is: "because you are reminded".

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ مِن أقْصى المَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعى﴾ ("and there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running"). This was a man who used to worship Allah in a cave in a mountain; when he heard of the messengers he came running — that is, hastening — to them, and said: "Do you want a wage for what you have brought?" The messengers said: "No." This man was called — according to what is related — "Ḥabīb the Carpenter". He turned to his people and said: ﴿يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوا المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ﴿اتَّبِعُوا مَن لا يَسْألُكم أجْرًا وهم مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 21], up to His saying: ﴿فاسْمَعُونِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 25]; so he made the messengers witnesses to his faith. Qatāda said: "This is a man who called his people to Allah and gave them sincere counsel, and they killed him for that; they set about stoning him while he was saying: O Allah, guide my people! O Allah, guide my people!" So Allah admitted him to Paradise, and he is alive in it, receiving provision. The meaning is: "when his people tormented him, it was said: Enter Paradise"; and when he beheld it he said: ﴿يا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 26] ﴿بِما غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وجَعَلَنِي مِنَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 27] ("would that my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured"), that is: [knew] of my Lord's forgiveness of me; “مِنَ المُكْرَمِينَ”, that is: among those admitted to Paradise. It has also been said: “بِما غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي”, that is: would that they knew the deeds and faith by which my Lord forgave me. And “بِمَ غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي” is permissible, in the sense: "for what thing my Lord forgave me"; and it is possible that “بِما” has this meaning with the alif retained: you say “قَدْ عَلِمْتُ بِما صَنَعْتَ هَذا” and “قَدْ عَلِمْتُ بِمَ صَنَعْتَ هَذا”, that is: "I know by what means you did this"; and dropping the alif in this sense is better.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿وَما أنْـزَلْنا عَلى قَوْمِهِ مِن بَعْدِهِ مِن جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ ("and We did not send down upon his people after him any host from heaven"). The meaning is: "We did not send down upon them a host; We did not take revenge with a host for the messenger whom they called a liar".

zajjaj:29-29.t: The meaning of ﴿إنْ كانَتْ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً﴾ ("it was but a single cry") is: "it was nothing but a single cry, nothing but that a single cry was cried at them, so they died, punished by it". It is also read: “إلّا صَيْحَةٌ واحِدَةٌ” [in the nominative]; Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī alone read it so, and it is good in Arabic. [Translator's note: the explanation that follows — "no punishment befell them except a single cry", which takes كانَ as complete with صَيْحَةٌ as its agent — fits the nominative reading, although the source introduces it with "whoever reads it in the accusative"; translated as written.] So whoever reads it in the accusative, the meaning is: "no punishment befell them except a single cry". ﴿فَإذا هم خامِدُونَ﴾ ("and at once they were extinguished"), that is: still; they had died and become like extinguished, lifeless ashes.

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿يا حَسْرَةً عَلى العِبادِ﴾ ("O the anguish for the servants!"). It has also been read: “يا حَسْرَةَ العِبادِ”, without “عَلى”; but I do not at all like reading with anything that differs from the muṣḥaf. This is one of the most difficult questions in the Qurʾān, when someone says: what is the benefit in calling out to anguish, when anguish is among the things that do not answer? The benefit in calling out to it is like the benefit in calling out to anything that does not reason, because the vocative (nidāʾ) is a means of alerting. When you say “يا زَيْدُ” ("O Zayd"), if you have not called him in order to address him with something other than the call, then the speech has no meaning; you only say "O Zayd" to alert him by the call, then you say to him: "you did such-and-such" or "do such-and-such", or whatever you like that has some benefit for him. Do you not see that you say to someone who is facing you: “يا زَيْدُ، ما أحْسَنَ ما صَنَعْتَ!” ("O Zayd, how excellent is what you did!")? If you had said to him: “ما أحْسَنَ ما صَنَعْتَ!”, you would have attained, in conveying the benefit, what you made him understand by it; except that your saying "O Zayd" is more emphatic in speech and more effective in making understood. Likewise, when you say to the one addressed: “أنا أعْجَبُ مِمّا فَعَلْتَ” ("I am amazed at what you did"), you have informed him that you are amazed; but if you said: “واعَجَباهُ مِمّا فَعَلْتَ!” ("O the wonder of what you did!") or “يا عَجَباهُ! أتَفْعَلُ كَذا وكَذا؟!” ("O wonder! Do you do such-and-such?!"), your calling out to wonder would be more effective in conveying the point. The meaning is: "O wonder, come forth, for this is one of your times!" Calling out to wonder is only an alerting, so that the one addressed is firmly made aware of the amazement at his deed. Likewise, when you say: “وَيْلٌ لِزَيْدٍ” or “وَيْلَ زَيْدٍ، لِمَ فَعَلَ كَذا وكَذا؟!” ("woe to Zayd, why did he do such-and-such?!"), it is more effective. And likewise in the Book of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ [Hūd: 72], and likewise: ﴿يا حَسْرَتا عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 56], and likewise: ﴿يا حَسْرَةً عَلى العِبادِ﴾. The meaning in the exegesis is that their mockery of the messengers is an anguish upon them. Ḥasra (anguish) is when a person is overcome, from the intensity of regret, by what has no end after it, until his heart remains exhausted (ḥasīr).

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِنَ القُرُونِ أنَّهم إلَيْهِمْ لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they will not return to them?"), that is: so that they fear that the like of what was hastened for others who were destroyed will be hastened for them in this world, and that, besides that, they will never return to this world. The position of “كَمْ” is accusative, governed by “أهْلَكْنا”, because “كَمْ” is not governed by what precedes it, whether it is declarative (khabar) or interrogative. You say in the declarative: “كَمْ سِرْتُ” ("how [far] I travelled!"), meaning: "I travelled many parasangs"; and “سِرْتُ كَمْ فَرْسَخًا” is not permissible. That is because “كَمْ” in its category is in the position of “رُبَّ”, and its origin is interrogation and vagueness. Just as when you ask and say to the one addressed: “كَمْ فَرْسَخًا سِرْتَ؟” ("how many parasangs did you travel?"), “سِرْتُ كَمْ فَرْسَخًا” is not permissible, because an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it — likewise when “كَمْ” is made declarative, the vagueness remains in it. “أنَّهم” is a badal (substitute) from the meaning of ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أهْلَكْنا﴾; the meaning is: "have they not seen, of the generations which We destroyed, that they do not return?" And “إنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ”, with kasra of “إنَّ”, is permissible; its meaning is resumption (istiʾnāf); the meaning is: "they will not return to them".

zajjaj:32-32.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنْ كُلٌّ لَمّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("and all of them will surely be brought before Us together"). Whoever reads with the light form, “لَما”, then “ما” is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic, and the meaning is: “إنْ كُلٌّ لَجَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ” ("all, indeed, will be brought before Us together"); its meaning is: "all are nothing but brought before Us together". It is also read “لَمّا” with shadda, and the meaning of “لَمّا” here is “ألّا” [i.e. إلّا, "except"]; you say: “سَألْتُكَ لَمّا فَعَلْتَ” ("I ask you [nothing] but that you do it"). The interpretation of the verse is that they will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and made to stand before what they did.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ الأرْضُ المَيْتَةُ أحْيَيْناها﴾ ("and a sign for them is the dead earth: We gave it life"). It is also read with shadda. The original of “اَلْمَيْتَةُ” is “اَلْمَيِّتَةُ”; the original is with shadda, and the light form is more common, and both are permissible. “آيَةٌ” is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is “لَهم”, that is: "and a sign for them, indicating to them the oneness of Allah and that Allah raises the dead, is the giving of life to the dead earth". It is also possible that “آيَةٌ” is nominative as mubtadaʾ and its khabar is “اَلْأرْضُ المَيْتَةُ”.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿وَفَجَّرْنا فِيها مِنَ العُيُونِ﴾ ﴿لِيَأْكُلُوا مِن ثَمَرِهِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 35] ("and We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they may eat of its fruit"). “ثُمْرِهِ” is also permissible, with sukūn on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ. ﴿وَما عَمِلَتْهُ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 35] ("and what their hands have made"): it is also read “عَمِلَتْ” without the hāʾ. The position of “ما” is genitive; the meaning is: "that they may eat of its fruit and of what their hands have made". It is also possible that “ما” is a negation, in the sense: "that they may eat of its fruit, while their hands did not make it" — this is with the hāʾ retained. When the hāʾ is dropped, the preferred analysis is that “ما” is in the position of a genitive and that “ما” is in the sense of “اَلَّذِي” ("that which"), so dropping the hāʾ is good; and this would be in line with His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 63] ﴿أأنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أمْ نَحْنُ الزّارِعُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 64].

zajjaj:36-36.t: And His saying: ﴿سُبْحانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الأزْواجَ كُلَّها﴾ ("glory be to Him who created all the pairs"). “سُبْحانَ” is declaring Allah free of every evil and exalting Him above it. The meaning of “اَلْأزْواجُ” is all the kinds — of plants, animals and others. ﴿وَمِن أنْفُسِهِمْ ومِمّا لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("and of themselves and of what they do not know"): of what Allah has created of all the species and likenesses.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنهُ النَّهارَ﴾ ("and a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it"). The meaning of “نَسْلَخُ” is: We bring the day out of it in such a way that nothing of the light of day remains with it; and that is among the signs that indicate the oneness of Allah and His power.

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿والشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَها﴾ ("and the sun runs to a resting place of its own"). The meaning is: "and a sign for them is the sun, running to a resting place of its own", that is: to a term that has been appointed for it and decreed for it. Whoever reads: “لا مُسْتَقَرَّ لَها” ("it has no resting place"), its meaning is that it runs forever and does not stay fixed in any place.

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿والقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ﴾ ("and the moon — We have determined for it phases"). It is read with the nominative and the accusative. Whoever reads the accusative takes it as: “وَقَدَّرْنا القَمَرَ مَنازِلَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ”; and the nominative is in the sense: “وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ القَمَرُ قَدَّرْناهُ” ("and a sign for them is the moon: We have determined it"); it is also possible that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and “قَدَّرْناهُ” the khabar (predicate). ﴿حَتّى عادَ كالعُرْجُونِ القَدِيمِ﴾ ("until it returns like an old date-stalk"). “اَلْعُرْجُونُ” is the stalk of the date-cluster which is called “اَلْكِباسَةُ”; the true sense of al-ʿurjūn is that it is the stalk on which the cluster hangs. “اَلْعُرْجُونُ” is the stalk of the cluster on which the sprigs of the cluster sit; when it dries and becomes old it becomes thin and small, and then it resembles the crescent moon at the end of the month and at its first rising. The pattern of “عُرْجُونٌ” is “فُعْلُولٌ”, from “اَلِانْعِراجُ” (bending).

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿لا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَها أنْ تُدْرِكَ القَمَرَ﴾ ("it is not for the sun to overtake the moon") — the verse. The meaning is: "neither of them takes away the meaning of the other". ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("and each is swimming in an orbit"): each one of them has an orbit. The meaning of “يَسْبَحُونَ” is: they travel in it with ease and expansiveness; and everyone who moves freely in something has "swum" in it; and from that is swimming in water.

zajjaj:41-41.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهم أنّا حَمَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهم في الفُلْكِ المَشْحُونِ﴾ ("and a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship"). The people of Mecca were addressed with this. It was said “حَمَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهم” ("We carried their offspring") because those who were carried with Noah — peace be upon him — in the ship are their forefathers, and their [descendants are their] offspring. “اَلْمَشْحُونُ” in the language means: filled. “شَحَنْتُ السَّفِينَةَ” — when I have filled it; and “شَحَنْتُ المَدِينَةَ” and “أشْحَنْتُها” — when I have filled it.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying: ﴿وَخَلَقْنا لَهم مِن مِثْلِهِ ما يَرْكَبُونَ﴾ ("and We created for them the like of it, which they ride"). The majority in the exegesis is that “مِن مِثْلِهِ” means: of the like of Noah's ship. It has also been said that by “مِن مِثْلِهِ” He means the camels, and that camels in the desert are in the position of ships at sea.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
﴿وَإنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهم فَلا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We could drown them, and there would be no one to answer their cry"), that is: there would be no helper for them.
﴿إلا رَحْمَةً مِنّا﴾ [Yā Sīn: 44] ("except as a mercy from Us") is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "they are not rescued except out of a mercy from Us and for enjoyment until a time — until the expiry of the appointed term".

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّقُوا ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيكم وما خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ ("and when it is said to them: Beware of what is before you and what is behind you"): what you have committed in the past of your sins, and what you will do in what lies ahead of you. It has also been said: “ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيكم وما خَلْفَكم” in the sense: "beware lest there descend upon you of punishment the like of what descended upon the nations before you"; “وَما خَلْفَكم”, that is: "beware of the punishment of the Hereafter". Similar to it is: ﴿فَإنْ أعْرَضُوا فَقُلْ أنْذَرْتُكم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 13].

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم أنْفِقُوا مِمّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ ("and when it is said to them: Spend of what Allah has provided you"), that is: "feed [others] and give charity". ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنُطْعِمُ مَن لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ أطْعَمَهُ﴾ ("those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would have fed?"): it is as though they say this by way of mockery. It has come in the exegesis that it was revealed concerning the zanādiqa (freethinkers), and it has been said: concerning a group of the Jews.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هَذا الوَعْدُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ ("and they say: When is this promise, if you are truthful?"): "When will this promise be fulfilled? Show it to us."

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿ما يَنْظُرُونَ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهم وهم يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾ ("they await nothing but a single cry which will seize them while they are disputing"). In “يَخِصِّمُونَ” there are four ways. [First,] sukūn of the khāʾ and the ṣād, with shadda on the ṣād, combining two quiescent letters; this is the harshest and worst of the four. One of those who transmit the reading of the people of Medina used to hold that this was not accurately recorded from the people of Medina, just as “إلى بارِئْكم” was not accurately recorded from Abū ʿAmr; he held that in this the vowel — the fatḥa of the khāʾ — is only slurred (ikhtilās), and the matter is as he said. The good reading is “يَخَصِّمُونَ”, with fatḥa on the khāʾ; the original is “يَخْتَصِمُونَ”: the fatḥa of the tāʾ was cast onto the khāʾ, and [the tāʾ] was assimilated into the ṣād. Kasra on the khāʾ is also good: the khāʾ is given a kasra because of its being quiescent along with the quiescence of the ṣād. It has also been read “يَخْتَصِمُونَ”, and that too is good. Its meaning is: "it seizes them while some of them dispute with others". It is also possible [that it means]: "it seizes them while they, among themselves, are disputing about the argument that they will not be raised; so the Hour comes while they are busy with their affairs".

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً﴾ ("then they will not be able to make a bequest"): no one will be able to give instructions about any of his affairs. ﴿وَلا إلى أهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("nor will they return to their families"): he will not remain [alive] until he gets to his family and his home; he dies in his place.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَنُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَإذا هم مِنَ الأجْداثِ إلى رَبِّهِمْ يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ ("and the trumpet will be blown, and at once from the graves they will hasten to their Lord"). “اَلصُّورُ”, as has come in the exegesis, is the horn into which Isrāfīl will blow. Abū ʿUbayda said that “اَلصُّورُ” is the plural of “صُورَةٌ” (form); but [the plural of] “صُورَةٌ” is “صُوَرٌ”, as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَصَوَّرَكم فَأحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 3], and no one read “أحْسَنَ صُورَكم”, nor did anyone read “وَنُفِخَ في الصُّوَرِ” by any established route. “اَلْأجْداثُ” are the graves; its singular is “جَدَثٌ”. “يَنْسِلُونَ” means: they come out quickly.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالُوا يا ويْلَنا مَن بَعَثَنا مِن مَرْقَدِنا﴾ ("they will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place?"): this is the complete stop (waqf al-tamām), and this is the saying of the polytheists.
And His saying: ﴿هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وصَدَقَ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾ ("this is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth"). “هَذا” is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is “ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ”; and this is the saying of the polytheists — I mean “هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ”. It is also possible that “هَذا” is a naʿt (adjective) of “مَرْقَدِنا”, in the sense: "Who has raised us from this sleeping place of ours in which we were sleeping?" Then “ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وصَدَقَ المُرْسَلُونَ” is on two accounts: one of them with “هَذا” implied, and the second with “حَقٌّ” ("true") implied, so that the meaning is: "true is what the Most Merciful promised". The first view — I mean that “هَذا” begins a new sentence — is what the exegesis holds, and it is the view of the philologists. [Translator's note: the source attributes «هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ» to the polytheists in both places; translated as written.]

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿إنْ كانَتْ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً﴾ ("it will be but a single cry"), and “إلّا صَيْحَةٌ واحِدَةٌ”; their i'rab has already been discussed. ﴿فَإذا هم جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("and at once they will all be brought before Us"). So the meaning is: "their destruction was by a cry, and their raising and revival is by a cry".

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿فاليَوْمَ لا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا ولا تُجْزَوْنَ إلا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("so today no soul will be wronged in anything, and you will be recompensed only for what you used to do"). The meaning is: "whoever is recompensed is recompensed only according to his deeds".

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿إنَّ أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ اليَوْمَ في شُغُلٍ فاكِهُونَ﴾ ("the people of Paradise today are busy in enjoyment"). The interpretation of “فاكِهُونَ” is “فَرِحُونَ” ("joyful"). It has come in the exegesis that their occupation is deflowering virgins; and it has been said: "occupied [and away] from what the people of the Fire are in". It is read “في شُغُلٍ” and “شُغْلٍ”; and “شُغْلٌ” and “شُغُلٌ” are permissible in Arabic.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿هم وأزْواجُهم في ظِلالٍ﴾ ("they and their spouses, in shades"), and “ظُلَلٍ”; “ظُلُلٍ” is also permissible.
﴿عَلى الأرائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾ ("reclining on couches"): these are the bedding-spreads in curtained canopies (ḥijāl). It has been said that they are the spreads, and it has been said: “اَلْأسِرَّةُ” ("the beds"). In reality they are “اَلْفُرُشُ” ("spreads"), whether in canopies or not in canopies.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿لَهم فِيها فاكِهَةٌ ولَهم ما يَدَّعُونَ﴾ ("they will have fruit therein, and they will have whatever they call for"), that is: whatever they wish for. It is said: “فُلانٌ في خَيْرِ ما ادَّعى” ("so-and-so is in the best of what he claimed"), that is: "what he wished for". It is taken from “اَلدُّعاءُ” (calling, supplication); the meaning is: "everything the people of Paradise call for comes to them".

zajjaj:58-58.t: ﴿سَلامٌ قَوْلا مِن رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾ ("Peace — a word from a Merciful Lord"). “سَلامٌ” is a badal (substitute) for “ما”; the meaning is: "they will have what they wish for: peace", that is: "and this is the wish of the people of Paradise — that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, should greet them with peace". “قَوْلًا” is accusative in the sense: "they will have peace, which Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — says as a word".

zajjaj:59-59.t: ﴿وامْتازُوا اليَوْمَ أيُّها المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ ("and stand apart today, O criminals"), that is: separate yourselves from the believers.

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿ألَمْ أعْهَدْ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ ("did I not enjoin upon you"). It is also read “أعْهِدْ” with kasra, and the fatḥa is more common, according to your saying “عَهِدَ، يَعْهَدُ”. The kasra is permissible on two accounts: on [the pattern] “عَهَدَ، يَعْهِدُ”, and on “عَهِدَ، يَعْهِدُ”, like “حَسِبَ، يَحْسِبُ”. Its meaning is: "Did I not lay upon you beforehand the covenant of faith and of abandoning the worship of Satan?"

zajjaj:62-62.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ أضَلَّ مِنكم جِبِلا﴾ ("and he has led astray a great multitude of you"). It is also read “جِبِلًّا”, with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ, and it is read “جُبُلًا”, with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ.
And it is read “جُبْلًا”, with sukūn on the bāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm. “جَبْلًا”, with fatḥa on the jīm, and “جِبْلًا”, with kasra on the jīm, are permissible; and “جِبَلًا”, with kasra on the jīm and fatḥa on the bāʾ, without shadda on the lām, is also permissible, as the plural of “جِبْلَةٌ” — [so] “جِبَلٌ”. “اَلْجِبْلَةُ”, in all of that, means: a great creation and many created beings.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَطَمَسْنا عَلى أعْيُنِهِمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We would have obliterated their eyes"). “اَلْمَطْمُوسُ” is the blind person whose eyelid cannot be distinguished, the edge of whose eye cannot be seen. That is: "if We willed We would have blinded them, so they would have strayed from the path — so how would they see if We did that to them?"

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَمَسَخْناهم عَلى مَكانَتِهِمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We would have transformed them in their places"), and “وَمَكاناتِهِمْ”; “اَلْمَكانَةُ” and “اَلْمَكانُ” have one meaning. ﴿فَما اسْتَطاعُوا مُضِيًّا ولا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("so they could neither go on nor turn back"), that is: they would be able neither to go nor to come.

zajjaj:68-68.t: ﴿وَمَن نُعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ﴾ ("and whomever We grant long life, We reverse him [in creation]"), and “نَنْكُسْهُ” and “نَنْكِسْهُ”; one says: “نَكَسْتُهُ، أنْكُسُهُ، وأنْكِسُهُ” — all of them. Its meaning is: "whomever We give a long life, We reverse his constitution", so that in place of strength there is weakness, and in place of youth decrepitude.

zajjaj:69-69.t: ﴿وَما عَلَّمْناهُ الشِّعْرَ وما يَنْبَغِي لَهُ﴾ ("and We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him"), that is: We did not teach Muḥammad ﷺ the composing of poetry, nor is it fitting for him, that is: it does not come easily to him. ﴿إنْ هو إلا ذِكْرٌ وقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ("it is only a Reminder and a clear Qurʾān"), that is: what the Prophet ﷺ brought, which the unbelievers claimed is poetry, is not poetry. This does not entail that the Prophet ﷺ never once quoted a verse of poetry; it only entails that the Prophet — peace be upon him — is not a poet, and that the Qurʾān which he brought is from Allah, because it is distinct from the speech of created beings and from the metres of the poetry of the Arabs. The Qurʾān is an inimitable sign, indicating that the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ and his signs are established forever.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَن كانَ حَيًّا﴾ ("that he may warn whoever is alive"). It is possible that the implied pronoun in His saying “لِيُنْذِرَ” is the Prophet — peace be upon him — and it is possible that it is the Qurʾān. The meaning of “مَن كانَ حَيًّا” is: whoever understands what he is addressed with; for the unbeliever is like the dead in that he has not reflected so as to know that the Prophet ﷺ and what he brought are true. ﴿وَيَحِقَّ القَوْلُ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ ("and that the word may come true against the unbelievers"); “وَيَحُقَّ القَوْلُ” is also permissible, that is: the proof is established against them. “لِتُنْذِرَ مَن كانَ حَيًّا”, with the tāʾ, is also permissible, as "an address to the Prophet ﷺ"; and “لِيَنْذَرَ”, that is: "that he may know", is permissible; one says: “نَذِرْتُ بِكَذا وكَذا، أنْذَرُ” ("I became aware of such-and-such"), like “عَلِمْتُ، أعْلَمُ”.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَهم لَها مالِكُونَ﴾ ("so they are its owners"): the meaning of “مالِكُونَ” is: in control [of them], because the intent here is that they are made submissive to them. Do you not see His saying: “وَذَلَّلْناها لَهم” ("and We have subdued them for them")? Similar to it in poetry:
؎أصْبَحْتُ لا أحْمِلُ السِّلاحَ ولا ∗∗∗ أمْلِكُ رَأْسَ البَعِيرِ إنْ نَفَرا
(I have come to be one who no longer bears arms, nor can I control the camel's head if it bolts.)
That is: I cannot control the camel's head.

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying: ﴿فَمِنها رَكُوبُهُمْ﴾ ("and of them are their mounts"): its meaning is: "what they ride"; and the evidence is the reading of whoever read: “فَمِنها رَكُوبَتُهم”. “رُكُوبُهم”, with ḍamma on the rāʾ, is also permissible, though I do not know anyone who read it so, in the sense: "of them is their riding, their eating and their drinking".

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿وَهم لَهم جُنْدٌ مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("while they are for them a host brought forth"), that is: they [the worshippers] rally to the support of the idols, while the idols are unable to help them.

zajjaj:78-78.t: And His saying: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ﴾ ("and he strikes for Us a parable and forgets his own creation") — the verse. It has come in the exegesis that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Prophet ﷺ with a decayed bone, crumbled it, then scattered it and said: "Who will give life to this?" So the answer to him was: ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79] ("say: He will give them life who produced them the first time"); for power in originating is clearer than in restoring. It is said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was the one in the story, and it is said: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.

zajjaj:81-81.t: And He informed them that the creation of the heavens and the earth is more far-reaching in power, and [that He has power] over reviving the dead; so He said: ﴿أوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ﴾ ("is not He who created the heavens and the earth…") — the verse. And He said in another place: ﴿لَخَلْقُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ أكْبَرُ مِن خَلْقِ النّاسِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 57].

zajjaj:83-83.t: And He said: ﴿فَسُبْحانَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ ("so glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things"): its meaning is declaring Allah free of every evil and of being described as anything other than powerful. ﴿الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, that is: power over everything. ﴿وَإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("and to Him you will be returned"), and “تَرْجِعُونَ” ("you will return"), that is: He will raise you after your death.
